findings.title: PORTUPDT applies update-file values to master with no validity checks
findings.description:
##### Overview
Values from UPDTFILE are moved straight into the master record without type, range or domain checks, then REWRITTEN.

##### Applicability
SI-10 requires validity checks on information inputs. The batch update file is an external input to the authoritative portfolio master.

##### Evidence
- Line 134: a 50-byte `UPDT-NEW-VALUE` is truncated into one-byte `PORT-STATUS` with no check against the A/C/S 88-levels.
- Line 136: client name is copied without a blank or content check.
- Lines 138-139: an alphanumeric value is MOVEd to numeric fields with no `IS NUMERIC` test, which can store corrupt values or raise a data exception on COMP-3 `PORT-TOTAL-VALUE`.
- Lines 132-142: an action code outside S/V/N falls through the EVALUATE (no WHEN OTHER) and still REWRITEs.

##### Impact
- Invalid statuses, blank names or corrupt valuations can be persisted to the master file used by online inquiry and reporting.
findings.recommendation: Validate each update before applying it: status must be one of the PORTFLIO 88-level values, the name must be non-blank, the value must pass an `IS NUMERIC`/`FUNCTION TEST-NUMVAL` check and a range check before conversion, and the action code must be valid (add WHEN OTHER). Reject and count invalid records without REWRITE.

snippets.commentary: Unvalidated update values are moved into master fields, followed by an unconditional REWRITE.
snippets.code:
2200-APPLY-UPDATE.
             EVALUATE TRUE
                 WHEN UPDT-STATUS
                     MOVE UPDT-NEW-VALUE TO PORT-STATUS
                 WHEN UPDT-NAME
                     MOVE UPDT-NEW-VALUE TO PORT-CLIENT-NAME
                 WHEN UPDT-VALUE
                     MOVE UPDT-NEW-VALUE TO WS-NUMERIC-WORK
                     MOVE WS-NUMERIC-WORK TO PORT-TOTAL-VALUE
             END-EVALUATE
             
             REWRITE PORT-RECORD

snippets.commentary: The update record layout has a free-form 50-byte new value.
snippets.code:
01  UPDATE-RECORD.
             05  UPDT-KEY.
                 10  UPDT-ID        PIC X(8).
                 10  UPDT-ACCT-NO   PIC X(10).
             05  UPDT-ACTION        PIC X(1).
                 88  UPDT-STATUS    VALUE 'S'.
                 88  UPDT-VALUE     VALUE 'V'.
                 88  UPDT-NAME      VALUE 'N'.
             05  UPDT-NEW-VALUE     PIC X(50).

findings.title: SECMGR AUDITLOG insert omits event outcome and accessed object
findings.description:
##### Overview
`P300-LOG-ACCESS` inserts timestamp, user, terminal, transaction, program and access type into AUDITLOG. It records no event outcome (success/failure) and no identity of the object accessed (account number). Because it is only called after a grant, it also cannot tell success from failure.

##### Applicability
AU-3 requires audit records to establish event type, time, location, source, outcome, and the identity of the individuals or subjects/objects involved. SECMGR writes the only online access audit record for the inquiry transaction.

##### Evidence
- Lines 117-125: the insert column list has no status/outcome column and no account or portfolio key. `PROGRAM` takes `SEC-RESOURCE-NAME`, which the caller always sets to the constant 'INQONLN'.
- The shared audit layout `src/copybook/common/AUDITLOG.cpy` already defines `AUD-STATUS` (line 27) and `AUD-ACCOUNT-NO` (line 33), and this insert does not fill them.

##### Impact
- AUDITLOG entries cannot show which client account was viewed or whether access was granted.
- Assumption: the DB2 AUDITLOG table has, or can be given, status and key columns. The DDL was not part of this batch.
findings.recommendation: Add outcome (SUCC/FAIL plus reason) and the accessed account/portfolio key to the SECMGR request area and AUDITLOG insert. Have callers log every decision, not only grants.

snippets.commentary: The audit insert carries no outcome and no accessed-object identifier.
snippets.code:
P300-LOG-ACCESS.
             MOVE FUNCTION CURRENT-DATE TO WS-TIMESTAMP.
             
             EXEC CICS ASSIGN
                       USERID(WS-USER-ID)
                       TERMID(WS-TERMINAL-ID)
                       TRANSID(WS-TRANSACTION-ID)
             END-EXEC.
             
             MOVE SEC-RESOURCE-NAME TO WS-PROGRAM-NAME.
             MOVE SEC-ACCESS-TYPE TO WS-ACCESS-TYPE.
             
             EXEC SQL
                  INSERT INTO AUDITLOG
                  (TIMESTAMP, USER_ID, TERMINAL_ID, 
                   TRANS_ID, PROGRAM, ACCESS_TYPE)
                  VALUES
                  (:WS-TIMESTAMP, :WS-USER-ID, :WS-TERMINAL-ID,
                   :WS-TRANSACTION-ID, :WS-PROGRAM-NAME, 
                   :WS-ACCESS-TYPE)
             END-EXEC.

snippets.commentary: The standard audit record defines status and account key fields that SECMGR's insert omits.
snippets.code:
05  AUD-STATUS           PIC X(4).
                 88  AUD-SUCCESS        VALUE 'SUCC'.
                 88  AUD-FAILURE        VALUE 'FAIL'.
                 88  AUD-WARNING        VALUE 'WARN'.
             05  AUD-KEY-INFO.
                 10  AUD-PORTFOLIO-ID  PIC X(8).
                 10  AUD-ACCOUNT-NO    PIC X(10).

findings.title: INQPORT returns positions for any COMMAREA account number without ownership check
findings.description:
##### Overview
INQPORT reads POSFILE using the account number from the COMMAREA, which INQONLN fills straight from the terminal map, and sends the record to the screen. Nothing checks whether the signed-on user may see that account. The only application authorization in the flow (SECMGR) works at program level (`INQONLN`/`READ`) and runs after INQPORT, per the INQONLN finding.

##### Applicability
AC-3 requires access to information to follow approved authorizations, and AC-6 requires access limited to what the user needs. Client portfolio positions are per-account data, and INQPORT is the component that reads and discloses them. Dataset-level ESM security (outside the repo) cannot restrict by account within one VSAM file.

##### Evidence
- Line 59: the COMMAREA is copied in as-is.
- Lines 68-82: `WS-COMMAREA-ACCOUNT-NO` becomes the RIDFLD for `READ FILE('POSFILE')`. There is no format check and no lookup of the user's entitlements.
- Lines 86-92: the record is sent to the terminal.
- SECMGR lines 78-101 authorize on `RESOURCE` (constant 'INQONLN') only, never on the account.

##### Impact
- Any user who can run PINQ can view another client's positions (units, cost basis, market value) by entering that client's account number.
- Assumption: no account-level entitlement source outside the repo is consulted. Nothing in the repo references one.
findings.recommendation: Before the POSFILE read, validate the account number's format, then authorize the signed-on user (EXEC CICS ASSIGN USERID) for that specific account. Do this through a SECMGR 'A' request with the account as the resource, an entitlement table, or EXEC CICS QUERY SECURITY on an account-level profile. Return a generic not-authorized message on denial and log the decision.

snippets.commentary: The caller-supplied account number goes straight to the VSAM read key.
snippets.code:
P100-INIT-PROGRAM.
             MOVE LOW-VALUES TO WS-POSITION-RECORD
             MOVE DFHCOMMAREA TO WS-COMMAREA.
             
             EXEC CICS HANDLE CONDITION
                       ERROR(P999-ERROR-ROUTINE)
                       NOTFND(P900-NOT-FOUND)
             END-EXEC.
         P100-EXIT.
             EXIT.
             
         P200-GET-POSITION.
             MOVE WS-COMMAREA-ACCOUNT-NO 
               TO POSITION-ACCOUNT OF WS-POSITION-RECORD.
               
             EXEC CICS READ FILE('POSFILE')
                       INTO(WS-POSITION-RECORD)
                       RIDFLD(POSITION-ACCOUNT OF WS-POSITION-RECORD)
                       RESP(WS-RESPONSE-CODE)
             END-EXEC.
             
             IF WS-RESPONSE-CODE = DFHRESP(NORMAL)
                SET POSITION-EXISTS TO TRUE
             ELSE
                SET NO-POSITION TO TRUE
             END-IF.
         P200-EXIT.
             EXIT.

snippets.commentary: The position record is sent to the user's terminal.
snippets.code:
P300-FORMAT-DISPLAY.
             EXEC CICS SEND MAP('POSMAP')
                       MAPSET('INQSET')
                       FROM(WS-POSITION-RECORD)
                       ERASE
                       RESP(WS-RESPONSE-CODE)
             END-EXEC.

snippets.commentary: AUTHFILE authorization is keyed by program resource name and access type only.
snippets.code:
P200-CHECK-AUTH.
             EXEC SQL
                  SELECT COUNT(*)
                  INTO :WS-DB2-AREA
                  FROM AUTHFILE
                  WHERE USER_ID = :SEC-USER-ID
                    AND RESOURCE = :SEC-RESOURCE-NAME
                    AND ACCESS_TYPE = :SEC-ACCESS-TYPE
             END-EXEC.
             
             EVALUATE SQLCODE
                 WHEN 0
                      IF WS-DB2-AREA > 0
                         MOVE 0 TO SEC-RESPONSE-CODE
                      ELSE
                         MOVE 'Access denied' 
                           TO SEC-ERROR-INFO
                         MOVE 8 TO SEC-RESPONSE-CODE
                      END-IF
                 WHEN OTHER
                      MOVE 'Authorization check failed' 
                        TO SEC-ERROR-INFO
                      MOVE 12 TO SEC-RESPONSE-CODE
             END-EVALUATE.

findings.title: Denied or failed inquiry access attempts are never written to AUDITLOG
findings.description:
##### Overview
INQONLN asks SECMGR to write an access record (`SEC-REQUEST-TYPE 'L'`) only when both validation and authorization succeed. Denied and failed attempts leave no audit record. When the audit write itself fails, the data has already been displayed, and the only response is a warning-level error routine and RETURN.

##### Applicability
AU-2/AU-12 call for audit records of the defined event types, and access-control decisions (successful and unsuccessful) are standard ones. AU-5 requires a response to audit logging failures. INQONLN is the code that decides which online access events get recorded.

##### Evidence
- Lines 151-169: the `'L'` log request sits inside two nested `IF SEC-RESPONSE-CODE = 0` blocks. A non-zero result from validate or authorize skips logging entirely.
- Lines 82-88: the only handling for a non-zero code, including SECMGR's 'Audit logging failed' (SECMGR lines 127-133), is `P900-ERROR-ROUTINE` (ERRHNDL with `ERR-WARNING`) plus RETURN, after the inquiry output was sent.

##### Impact
- No record exists of unauthorized attempts to view portfolio or history data.
- An audit-write failure does not stop disclosure and raises no alert beyond a warning.
- Not verified: whether ERRHNDL's error log is reviewed or alerted on.
findings.recommendation: Call SECMGR 'L' on every decision, passing an outcome indicator (granted, denied validation, denied authorization) so AUDITLOG records failed attempts too. Do the log write before the inquiry, and when the audit write fails, deny the inquiry and raise an abend/critical condition through ERRHNDL instead of a warning.

snippets.commentary: The audit ('L') call can only be reached after a successful validate and authorize.
snippets.code:
IF SEC-RESPONSE-CODE = 0
                MOVE 'A' TO SEC-REQUEST-TYPE
                MOVE 'INQONLN' TO SEC-RESOURCE-NAME
                MOVE 'READ' TO SEC-ACCESS-TYPE
                
                EXEC CICS LINK PROGRAM('SECMGR')
                          COMMAREA(WS-SECURITY-REQUEST)
                          LENGTH(LENGTH OF WS-SECURITY-REQUEST)
                END-EXEC
                
                IF SEC-RESPONSE-CODE = 0
                   MOVE 'L' TO SEC-REQUEST-TYPE
                   
                   EXEC CICS LINK PROGRAM('SECMGR')
                             COMMAREA(WS-SECURITY-REQUEST)
                             LENGTH(LENGTH OF WS-SECURITY-REQUEST)
                   END-EXEC
                END-IF
             END-IF.

snippets.commentary: All failures, audit failure included, are handled only as an error routine and RETURN.
snippets.code:
IF SEC-RESPONSE-CODE NOT = 0
                MOVE SEC-ERROR-INFO 
                  TO WS-ERROR-MESSAGE
                PERFORM P900-ERROR-ROUTINE
                   THRU P900-EXIT
                EXEC CICS RETURN END-EXEC
             END-IF.

snippets.commentary: SECMGR reports an audit insert failure through SEC-RESPONSE-CODE 12.
snippets.code:
IF SQLCODE = 0
                MOVE 0 TO SEC-RESPONSE-CODE
             ELSE
                MOVE 'Audit logging failed' 
                  TO SEC-ERROR-INFO
                MOVE 12 TO SEC-RESPONSE-CODE
             END-IF.

findings.title: SECMGR authorization stores COUNT(*) into SQLCA group and compares group
findings.description:
##### Overview
`P200-CHECK-AUTH` selects `COUNT(*)` INTO `:WS-DB2-AREA`, the 01-level group that holds the SQLCA, and then makes the grant decision with `IF WS-DB2-AREA > 0`. That is an alphanumeric group comparison, not a test of an integer count. The access decision does not reliably reflect AUTHFILE contents and may fail open. The exact runtime result depends on precompiler/compiler handling, which I did not run.

##### Applicability
AC-3 requires enforcement of approved authorizations. SECMGR is the application's central access-decision routine for the online inquiry programs.

##### Evidence
- Lines 15-16: `WS-DB2-AREA` contains only `INCLUDE SQLCA`.
- Lines 79-86: the COUNT is written into that group, so the SQLCA itself is overlaid.
- Lines 88-101: `WS-DB2-AREA > 0` compares the group, which starts with SQLCAID text, against zero as alphanumeric. Non-blank text compares greater than '0', so any `SQLCODE = 0` result can come out as a grant whatever the count is.
- Lines 42-52: the EVALUATE has no `WHEN OTHER`, so an unrecognised request type returns with whatever `SEC-RESPONSE-CODE` the caller passed in (INQONLN never initializes it).

##### Impact
- Users with no AUTHFILE row may be authorized for `INQONLN READ`.
- Unknown request types are not denied by default.
- Not verified: compiled behaviour. Validation should test a user absent from AUTHFILE.
findings.recommendation: Declare a dedicated `WS-AUTH-COUNT PIC S9(9) COMP` host variable, select COUNT(*) INTO it, and grant only when `SQLCODE = 0 AND WS-AUTH-COUNT > 0`. Add `WHEN OTHER` that sets a deny response code, and initialize SEC-RESPONSE-CODE to non-zero at entry so all paths fail closed.

snippets.commentary: The host-variable target is the SQLCA group, not an integer field.
snippets.code:
01  WS-DB2-AREA.
             EXEC SQL INCLUDE SQLCA END-EXEC.

snippets.commentary: COUNT(*) goes into the SQLCA group, and the grant is decided by a group comparison.
snippets.code:
P200-CHECK-AUTH.
             EXEC SQL
                  SELECT COUNT(*)
                  INTO :WS-DB2-AREA
                  FROM AUTHFILE
                  WHERE USER_ID = :SEC-USER-ID
                    AND RESOURCE = :SEC-RESOURCE-NAME
                    AND ACCESS_TYPE = :SEC-ACCESS-TYPE
             END-EXEC.
             
             EVALUATE SQLCODE
                 WHEN 0
                      IF WS-DB2-AREA > 0
                         MOVE 0 TO SEC-RESPONSE-CODE
                      ELSE
                         MOVE 'Access denied' 
                           TO SEC-ERROR-INFO
                         MOVE 8 TO SEC-RESPONSE-CODE
                      END-IF
                 WHEN OTHER
                      MOVE 'Authorization check failed' 
                        TO SEC-ERROR-INFO
                      MOVE 12 TO SEC-RESPONSE-CODE
             END-EVALUATE.

snippets.commentary: There is no WHEN OTHER, so unknown request types do not fail closed.
snippets.code:
PROCEDURE DIVISION USING SECURITY-REQUEST-AREA.
             EVALUATE TRUE
                 WHEN SEC-VALIDATE
                      PERFORM P100-VALIDATE-USER
                         THRU P100-EXIT
                 WHEN SEC-AUTHORIZE
                      PERFORM P200-CHECK-AUTH
                         THRU P200-EXIT
                 WHEN SEC-AUDIT
                      PERFORM P300-LOG-ACCESS
                         THRU P300-EXIT
             END-EVALUATE.

findings.title: PORTUPDT DISPLAYs portfolio key with client account number to SYSOUT
findings.description:
##### Overview
On not-found and rewrite-failure, PORTUPDT DISPLAYs `PORT-KEY` (portfolio ID plus 10-digit client account number) to SYSOUT, which the JCL routes to `SYSOUT=*` with `MSGCLASS=X`. Whether that output class is access-restricted and how long it is kept is set by JES/ESM configuration outside the repo.

##### Applicability
SI-11 requires error messages to reveal sensitive information only to authorized personnel, and SI-12 covers retention of system output. Account numbers are client financial identifiers.

##### Evidence
- Lines 127 and 148: `PORT-KEY` is DISPLAYed in error messages.
- JCL lines 8 and 14-16 route the output to SYSOUT.

##### Impact
- Client account numbers appear in job output viewable by anyone with access to that JES output class.
- Not verified: JES output class protection and spool retention.
findings.recommendation: DISPLAY only the portfolio ID (or a masked account number) and the input record sequence number, and write full keys only to a protected error/audit dataset.

snippets.commentary: Error DISPLAYs include the full PORT-KEY with the account number.
snippets.code:
2100-PROCESS-UPDATE.
             MOVE UPDT-KEY TO PORT-KEY
             
             READ PORTFOLIO-FILE
             
             IF WS-SUCCESS-STATUS
                 PERFORM 2200-APPLY-UPDATE
             ELSE
                 ADD 1 TO WS-ERROR-COUNT
                 DISPLAY 'Record not found: ' PORT-KEY
             END-IF
             .
             
         2200-APPLY-UPDATE.
             EVALUATE TRUE
                 WHEN UPDT-STATUS
                     MOVE UPDT-NEW-VALUE TO PORT-STATUS
                 WHEN UPDT-NAME
                     MOVE UPDT-NEW-VALUE TO PORT-CLIENT-NAME
                 WHEN UPDT-VALUE
                     MOVE UPDT-NEW-VALUE TO WS-NUMERIC-WORK
                     MOVE WS-NUMERIC-WORK TO PORT-TOTAL-VALUE
             END-EVALUATE
             
             REWRITE PORT-RECORD
             
             IF WS-SUCCESS-STATUS
                 ADD 1 TO WS-UPDATE-COUNT
             ELSE
                 ADD 1 TO WS-ERROR-COUNT
                 DISPLAY 'Update failed for: ' PORT-KEY
             END-IF
             .

snippets.commentary: Program output goes to SYSOUT with MSGCLASS=X.

findings.title: INQONLN dispatches portfolio and history inquiries before running SECMGR checks
findings.description:
##### Overview
In each loop of `P100-PROCESS-REQUEST`, INQONLN runs the requested function (LINK to INQPORT/INQHIST, which read and SEND position/history data) and only afterwards calls `P050-SECURITY-CHECK`. The SECMGR validate/authorize decision therefore cannot stop the disclosure it is meant to gate. Any CICS transaction-level security on PINQ (RACF/ESM, outside this repo) is not visible here.

##### Applicability
AC-3 requires that approved authorizations are enforced before logical access to information is granted. INQONLN is the only entry program of transaction PINQ (`src/cics/PORTDFN.csd`) and is where the application's own authorization (SECMGR resource `INQONLN`/`READ`) is invoked. Signon and transaction-attach security are handled by CICS/ESM configuration outside the repo.

##### Evidence
- Lines 62-77: the EVALUATE on `WS-COMMAREA-FUNCTION` performs `P300-PORTFOLIO-INQUIRY` / `P400-HISTORY-INQUIRY` right away.
- Lines 79-88: `P050-SECURITY-CHECK` runs only after that, and a non-zero `SEC-RESPONSE-CODE` causes a RETURN once the data has already been sent.
- Lines 101-117: the LINKs pass the terminal-supplied COMMAREA (account number) to INQPORT/INQHIST. INQPORT sends the position map at its lines 86-92.

```
RECEIVE MAP --> LINK INQPORT/INQHIST --> SEND MAP (data shown) --> SECMGR V/A --> deny => RETURN
```

##### Impact
- Portfolio positions and transaction history for any account number typed on the screen are shown to users who would fail the SECMGR `AUTHFILE` check.
- The application-level access decision has no effect on disclosure. Only ESM transaction security (not verifiable here) gates PINQ.
- Assumption: INQPORT/INQHIST do no checks of their own. I confirmed this for INQPORT, and INQHIST has no SECMGR call.
findings.recommendation: Run P050-SECURITY-CHECK right after RECEIVE MAP and before the EVALUATE dispatch. Perform the INQP/INQH branches only when validate and authorize both return 0, and on denial send a generic error map and stop without LINKing to INQPORT/INQHIST. Initialize WS-SECURITY-REQUEST (including SEC-RESPONSE-CODE) before each check.

snippets.commentary: Inquiry functions are dispatched first, with no prior authorization decision.
snippets.code:
EVALUATE WS-COMMAREA-FUNCTION
                 WHEN 'MENU'
                      PERFORM P200-DISPLAY-MENU
                         THRU P200-EXIT
                 WHEN 'INQP'
                      PERFORM P300-PORTFOLIO-INQUIRY
                         THRU P300-EXIT
                 WHEN 'INQH'
                      PERFORM P400-HISTORY-INQUIRY
                         THRU P400-EXIT
                 WHEN 'EXIT'
                      SET SESSION-TERMINATED TO TRUE
                 WHEN OTHER
                      PERFORM P900-ERROR-ROUTINE
                         THRU P900-EXIT
             END-EVALUATE.

snippets.commentary: The security check and deny-RETURN run only after the inquiry has completed.
snippets.code:
PERFORM P050-SECURITY-CHECK
                THRU P050-EXIT.
                
             IF SEC-RESPONSE-CODE NOT = 0
                MOVE SEC-ERROR-INFO 
                  TO WS-ERROR-MESSAGE
                PERFORM P900-ERROR-ROUTINE
                   THRU P900-EXIT
                EXEC CICS RETURN END-EXEC
             END-IF.

snippets.commentary: P050 performs validate, authorize, and log through SECMGR.
snippets.code:
P050-SECURITY-CHECK.
             MOVE 'V' TO SEC-REQUEST-TYPE.
             
             EXEC CICS ASSIGN
                       USERID(SEC-USER-ID)
             END-EXEC.
             
             EXEC CICS LINK PROGRAM('SECMGR')
                       COMMAREA(WS-SECURITY-REQUEST)
                       LENGTH(LENGTH OF WS-SECURITY-REQUEST)
             END-EXEC.
             
             IF SEC-RESPONSE-CODE = 0
                MOVE 'A' TO SEC-REQUEST-TYPE
                MOVE 'INQONLN' TO SEC-RESOURCE-NAME
                MOVE 'READ' TO SEC-ACCESS-TYPE
                
                EXEC CICS LINK PROGRAM('SECMGR')
                          COMMAREA(WS-SECURITY-REQUEST)
                          LENGTH(LENGTH OF WS-SECURITY-REQUEST)
                END-EXEC
                
                IF SEC-RESPONSE-CODE = 0
                   MOVE 'L' TO SEC-REQUEST-TYPE
                   
                   EXEC CICS LINK PROGRAM('SECMGR')
                             COMMAREA(WS-SECURITY-REQUEST)
                             LENGTH(LENGTH OF WS-SECURITY-REQUEST)
                   END-EXEC
                END-IF
             END-IF.
         P050-EXIT.
             EXIT.

snippets.commentary: The LINKed INQPORT sends the position map to the terminal.
snippets.code:
P300-FORMAT-DISPLAY.
             EXEC CICS SEND MAP('POSMAP')
                       MAPSET('INQSET')
                       FROM(WS-POSITION-RECORD)
                       ERASE
                       RESP(WS-RESPONSE-CODE)
             END-EXEC.

findings.title: PORTMSTR 2100-VALIDATE-PORTFOLIO checks ID format, name and status
findings.description:
##### Artifact
`2100-VALIDATE-PORTFOLIO` (lines 138-161) rejects records whose PORT-ID does not start with 'PORT' followed by five numeric characters, whose PORT-NAME is blank, or whose PORT-STATUS is not A/I/C. Create (line 121) and update (line 189) run it before `WRITE`/`REWRITE`. Read (163-181) and delete (209-226) use the caller-supplied key without running it.

##### Bears on
SI-10 (validity checks on information inputs) for portfolio master maintenance inputs passed in `LS-PORTFOLIO`.

##### Limits
PORT-TOTAL-VALUE and PORT-CREATE-DATE are not validated. The checked status set (A/I/C) differs from the PORTFLIO copybook's 88-levels (A/C/S), and PORTMSTR's own 100-byte record layout differs from PORTFLIO.

snippets.commentary: Field-level validation is applied to create and update input.
snippets.code:
2100-VALIDATE-PORTFOLIO.
        *----------------------------------------------------------------*
        * Validate portfolio data
        *----------------------------------------------------------------*
             IF PORT-ID(1:4) NOT = 'PORT'
                OR PORT-ID(5:5) IS NOT NUMERIC
                 MOVE 'Invalid Portfolio ID format' TO WS-ERROR-TEXT
                 MOVE WS-ERROR TO WS-RETURN-CODE
                 EXIT PARAGRAPH
             END-IF
             
             IF PORT-NAME = SPACES
                 MOVE 'Portfolio Name is required' TO WS-ERROR-TEXT
                 MOVE WS-ERROR TO WS-RETURN-CODE
                 EXIT PARAGRAPH
             END-IF
             
             MOVE PORT-STATUS TO WS-VALID-STATUS
             IF NOT VALID-STATUS
                 MOVE 'Invalid Portfolio Status' TO WS-ERROR-TEXT
                 MOVE WS-ERROR TO WS-RETURN-CODE
                 EXIT PARAGRAPH
             END-IF
             .

findings.title: SECMGR audit timestamp sourced from FUNCTION CURRENT-DATE
findings.description:
##### Artifact
Line 106 moves `FUNCTION CURRENT-DATE` (21 characters: YYYYMMDDHHMMSShh plus a signed GMT offset) into `WS-TIMESTAMP PIC X(26)`. That value is inserted into the AUDITLOG `TIMESTAMP` column (lines 117-125).

##### Bears on
AU-8 (time stamps from internal system clocks, with granularity and UTC mapping). The value has hundredth-of-second granularity and carries the local-to-GMT offset. Clock synchronization of the z/OS system must be evidenced from platform configuration outside the repo.

##### Limits
The DB2 column type for TIMESTAMP is not shown here, so conversion behaviour of the 21-character string on insert is not shown.

snippets.commentary: The audit timestamp comes from FUNCTION CURRENT-DATE.
snippets.code:
P300-LOG-ACCESS.
             MOVE FUNCTION CURRENT-DATE TO WS-TIMESTAMP.

snippets.commentary: The timestamp value is inserted into AUDITLOG.
snippets.code:
EXEC SQL
                  INSERT INTO AUDITLOG
                  (TIMESTAMP, USER_ID, TERMINAL_ID, 
                   TRANS_ID, PROGRAM, ACCESS_TYPE)
                  VALUES
                  (:WS-TIMESTAMP, :WS-USER-ID, :WS-TERMINAL-ID,
                   :WS-TRANSACTION-ID, :WS-PROGRAM-NAME, 
                   :WS-ACCESS-TYPE)
             END-EXEC.

findings.title: SECMGR user validation compares ASSIGN USERID against caller-copied USERID
findings.description:
##### Artifact
`P100-VALIDATE-USER` (lines 56-75) issues `EXEC CICS ASSIGN USERID` and compares the result to `SEC-USER-ID`. The caller INQONLN (lines 142-144) filled that field from the same `ASSIGN USERID`. No password, authenticator, ESM verify/signon call, or failed-attempt counter appears anywhere in the program. User identity comes from whatever CICS signon established for the task.

##### Bears on
IA-2 (identification and authentication), AC-7 (invalid logon attempt limit and lockout), and IA-5 (authenticator management). These lines hand authentication to the CICS region's signon and external security manager (e.g. RACF). Password policy, the consecutive-failure limit and lockout must be evidenced from the ESM and CICS SIT/signon configuration, which are not in this repository.

##### Limits
The code does not show whether PINQ requires a signed-on user (rather than the CICS default user), or any ESM settings.

snippets.commentary: The validate step compares the CICS-assigned USERID with a caller-copied value.
snippets.code:
P100-VALIDATE-USER.
             EXEC CICS ASSIGN
                       USERID(WS-USER-ID)
                       RESP(SEC-RESPONSE-CODE)
             END-EXEC.
             
             IF SEC-RESPONSE-CODE = DFHRESP(NORMAL)
                IF SEC-USER-ID = WS-USER-ID
                   MOVE 0 TO SEC-RESPONSE-CODE
                ELSE
                   MOVE 'User validation failed' 
                     TO SEC-ERROR-INFO
                   MOVE 8 TO SEC-RESPONSE-CODE
                END-IF
             ELSE
                MOVE 'Unable to obtain user credentials' 
                  TO SEC-ERROR-INFO
                MOVE 12 TO SEC-RESPONSE-CODE
             END-IF.
         P100-EXIT.

snippets.commentary: The caller fills SEC-USER-ID from the same ASSIGN USERID before LINKing SECMGR.

findings.title: PORTMSTR create and delete leave no audit record; update audit broken
findings.description:
##### Overview
PORTMSTR creates (`WRITE`), updates (`REWRITE`) and deletes (`DELETE`) portfolio master records. Only the update path calls the audit routine. `2100-LOG-PORTFOLIO-UPDATE` refers to data items PORTMSTR never defines and records no real before-image, and the AUDPROC return code is ignored.

##### Applicability
AU-2/AU-12 require audit records for the defined events. Create, update and delete of the authoritative portfolio master are the core audited events in this system (the AUDITLOG layout defines CREATE/UPDATE/DELETE actions). AU-3 requires the record content, and AU-5 requires a response when logging fails.

##### Evidence
- Lines 115-136 (create, `WRITE` at 126) and 209-226 (delete, `DELETE` at 215) contain no `CALL 'AUDPROC'`.
- Line 206: update performs `2100-LOG-PORTFOLIO-UPDATE`. In that paragraph (lines 268-288), `LS-AUDIT-REQUEST`, `USERID`, `TERMINAL-ID`, `WS-BEFORE-IMAGE`, `PORT-ACCOUNT-NO`, `PORT-RECORD` and the `LS-*` targets are not declared in PORTMSTR's WORKING-STORAGE or LINKAGE (lines 41-80). No before-image is captured before the `REWRITE` at 194.
- Line 287: the call result is never checked.
- Lines 243-263 reuse the `2100-` paragraph prefix with further undefined items, which suggests template code that was never integrated.

##### Impact
- Portfolio creation and deletion, including irreversible removal of master records, leave no trace of who did what.
- Updates cannot produce a valid before/after record, and failed audit writes go unnoticed.
- Assumption: callers of PORTMSTR do not write their own audit records. None was found in this batch.
findings.recommendation: Declare the AUDPROC request area (matching AUDPROC's LS-AUDIT-REQUEST) and a before-image buffer in PORTMSTR. READ the existing record before REWRITE/DELETE to capture the before-image, obtain the user and terminal IDs from the caller or the execution environment, and call AUDPROC with action CREATE/UPDATE/DELETE and SUCC/FAIL status on every mutation path, failures included. Check the AUDPROC return code and fail the operation (or raise a critical error) when the audit write fails.

findings.title: PORTUPDT batch REWRITEs portfolio master without any audit record
findings.description:
##### Overview
PORTUPDT applies sequential update transactions (status, client name, total value) to the portfolio master with `REWRITE`. It writes no audit record and does not update the record's own `PORT-LAST-USER`/`PORT-LAST-TRANS` fields, so each change leaves no who/what/before/after trace.

##### Applicability
AU-2/AU-12 require audit records for the defined event types, and AU-3 requires their content. Changes to the authoritative portfolio master, including client name and holdings value, are audited event types per the AUDITLOG UPDATE action, and AUDPROC exists for this purpose.

##### Evidence
- Lines 131-150: `2200-APPLY-UPDATE` overwrites fields and `REWRITE`s (line 142) with no AUDPROC call and no before-image saved.
- The only output is SYSOUT counters (lines 156-157).
- The JCL `src/jcl/portfolio/PORTUPDT.jcl` allocates no audit dataset.

##### Impact
- Bulk changes to client names, account status and valuations cannot be traced to a job, a user, or prior values.
- Assumption: no external SMF/ESM logging is relied on for record-level change history. That would record dataset access only, not field changes.
findings.recommendation: Before each REWRITE, copy the read record to a before-image. After the REWRITE, call AUDPROC with system/user (job or ESM user), program PORTUPDT, action UPDATE, SUCC/FAIL status, the PORT-KEY, and the before/after images. Set PORT-LAST-USER/PORT-LAST-TRANS, check AUDPROC's return code, and stop with a non-zero RC if auditing fails.

                 WHEN UPDT-VALUE

             ELSE

findings.title: RTNCDE00 return-code audit trail drops UTC offset and user identity
findings.description:
##### Overview

RTNCDE00 documents itself as maintaining a return-code audit trail in DB2 RTNCODES, but the timestamp it inserts is truncated to local date/time without the GMT offset and the row carries no user or job identity.

##### Applicability

AU-8 (timestamps mappable to UTC) and AU-3 (records establish who/what) apply to rows this program describes as an audit trail.

##### Evidence

Line 94 moves FUNCTION CURRENT-DATE (21 bytes, offset in positions 17-21) into WS-CURRENT-TIME, a 16-byte group (lines 15-23), discarding the offset; lines 96-111 insert that value plus program ID, codes, status and message only. Insert failure (lines 113-117) only sets RC-RESPONSE-CODE 8.

##### Impact

- Return-code records cannot be correlated to UTC or to a user/job.
- Assumption: RTNCODES is used as audit evidence as the header states.
findings.recommendation: Extend WS-CURRENT-TIME to 21 bytes (or use DB2 CURRENT TIMESTAMP with CURRENT TIMEZONE / store UTC) and add job name and user ID columns populated from the job/RACF environment.

             05 WS-CURRENT-DATE.
                10 WS-CURRENT-YEAR     PIC 9(4).
                10 WS-CURRENT-MONTH    PIC 9(2).
                10 WS-CURRENT-DAY      PIC 9(2).
             05 WS-CURRENT-HOURS       PIC 9(2).
             05 WS-CURRENT-MINUTES     PIC 9(2).
             05 WS-CURRENT-SECONDS     PIC 9(2).
             05 WS-CURRENT-MILLISEC    PIC 9(2).

snippets.code:
P400-LOG-RETURN-CODE.
             MOVE FUNCTION CURRENT-DATE TO WS-CURRENT-TIME.
             
             EXEC SQL
                  INSERT INTO RTNCODES
                  (TIMESTAMP,
                   PROGRAM_ID,
                   RETURN_CODE,
                   HIGHEST_CODE,
                   STATUS_CODE,
                   MESSAGE_TEXT)
                  VALUES
                  (:WS-CURRENT-TIME,
                   :RC-PROGRAM-ID,
                   :RC-CURRENT-CODE,
                   :RC-HIGHEST-CODE,
                   :RC-STATUS,
                   :RC-MESSAGE)
             END-EXEC.
             
             IF SQLCODE = 0
                MOVE 0 TO RC-RESPONSE-CODE
             ELSE
                MOVE 8 TO RC-RESPONSE-CODE
             END-IF.
         P400-EXIT.
             EXIT.

findings.title: PORTTRAN passes AUDIT-RECORD layout to AUDPROC's shifted request layout
findings.description:
##### Overview

AUDPROC's LS-AUDIT-REQUEST begins with system/user/program/terminal, but PORTTRAN calls it with the AUDITLOG AUDIT-RECORD, which begins with a 26-byte timestamp, so every field AUDPROC copies from a PORTTRAN call is offset by 26 bytes.

##### Applicability

AU-3 requires audit records to establish event type, time, source, outcome and identity. The interface contract of the central audit writer determines record content for every caller.

##### Evidence

AUDPROC lines 34-49 define the request starting with LS-SYSTEM-ID; AUDITLOG.cpy lines 7-36 start AUDIT-RECORD with AUD-TIMESTAMP X(26). PORTTRAN line 294 passes AUDIT-RECORD. AUDPROC lines 75-82 then move LS-SYSTEM-INFO (timestamp bytes) into AUD-HEADER's system/user/program/terminal and shift type, action, status, key and images. AUD-HEADER also includes AUD-TIMESTAMP, so line 75 overwrites the timestamp set at line 74.

##### Impact

- PORTTRAN audit records have wrong user ID, program, action, status and account key; the record's own timestamp is overwritten by the move of LS-SYSTEM-INFO into AUD-HEADER for all callers.
- Not verified: PORTMSTR's LS-AUDIT-REQUEST layout matches AUDPROC (other batch).
findings.recommendation: Define the request layout in a shared copybook used by AUDPROC and all callers; move LS-SYSTEM-INFO to the individual AUD-SYSTEM-ID..AUD-TERMINAL fields (not AUD-HEADER) after setting AUD-TIMESTAMP; change PORTTRAN to build and pass the request structure.

findings.title: RCVPRC00 recovery resets completed jobs and restarts without limit
findings.description:
##### Overview

Recovery rewrites batch-control status for each selected process without checking its current state, so 'S'/'A' recovery resets DONE processes to READY or forces DONE on failed ones; restartable processes are restarted with no max-restart check. No program currently CALLs RCVPRC00.

##### Applicability

SC-24 (fail to a known state preserving state information) and SI-7 (information integrity) apply to the operator recovery handler that changes batch-control state driving which jobs PRCSEQ00 runs next.

##### Evidence

Lines 159-171: 2100-RECOVER-PROCESS reads the record and acts without testing BCT-STATUS. Lines 182-190: the BCT-MAX-RESTARTS test runs only for non-restartable processes; restartable ones always restart. Lines 217-227: bypass marks a process DONE with RC 4, which PRCSEQ00 2210-CHECK-DEP-STATUS treats as satisfied when PSR-DEP-RC >= 4. Lines 263-281: recover-all walks every record regardless of date.

##### Impact

- Completed jobs can be re-queued and rerun, duplicating postings; failed jobs can be bypassed so dependents run on incomplete data.
- Unbounded restart loops for restartable jobs.
- Not verified: how operators invoke RCVPRC00 (no caller in repo).
findings.recommendation: Only act on processes in ERROR/ACTIVE (abended) state, apply BCT-MAX-RESTARTS to all restarts, require an explicit operator flag for bypass and record it, and restrict recover-all to the requested process date.

snippets.commentary: Recovery acts without checking current process status.

2100-RECOVER-PROCESS.
             MOVE LS-PROCESS-ID   TO BCT-JOB-NAME
             MOVE LS-PROCESS-DATE TO BCT-PROCESS-DATE
             
             READ BATCH-CONTROL-FILE
                 INVALID KEY
                     MOVE 'Process record not found' TO ERR-TEXT
                     PERFORM 9000-ERROR-ROUTINE
             END-READ
             
             PERFORM 2110-DETERMINE-ACTION
             PERFORM 2120-EXECUTE-RECOVERY
             .

snippets.commentary: Max-restart limit only applied to non-restartable processes.
snippets.code:

             MOVE LS-PROCESS-ID TO PSR-PROCESS-ID
             
             READ PROCESS-SEQ-FILE
                 INVALID KEY
                     MOVE 'Process definition not found' TO ERR-TEXT
                     PERFORM 9000-ERROR-ROUTINE
             END-READ
             
             IF PSR-RESTARTABLE
                 SET WS-ACTION-RESTART TO TRUE
             ELSE
                 IF BCT-RESTART-COUNT > BCT-MAX-RESTARTS
                     SET WS-ACTION-TERMINATE TO TRUE
                 ELSE
                     SET WS-ACTION-BYPASS TO TRUE
                 END-IF
             END-IF
             .

findings.title: DB2CONN disconnect unconditionally commits pending work
findings.description:
##### Overview

The DISC function issues COMMIT WORK before CONNECT RESET regardless of the caller's state and without checking its SQLCODE, so a caller disconnecting after an error commits partial work.

##### Applicability

SC-24 requires failing to a known state; a shared disconnect service that commits implicitly can persist an incomplete unit of work.

##### Evidence

Lines 109-117: COMMIT WORK then CONNECT RESET; only the CONNECT RESET SQLCODE is checked (line 119). There is no parameter allowing ROLLBACK on disconnect.

##### Impact

- Partial DB2 updates from a failed batch run can be committed at termination.
- Not verified: which callers use DB2CONN DISC (HISTLD00 uses DBPROC's DISCONNECT-FROM-DB2).
findings.recommendation: Remove the implicit COMMIT (require callers to commit through DB2CMT) or add a disposition flag defaulting to ROLLBACK, and check SQLCODE of the commit.

snippets.commentary: Disconnect path with implicit commit.
snippets.code:
2000-DISCONNECT.
             IF WS-CONNECTED
                 EXEC SQL
                     COMMIT WORK
                 END-EXEC
                 
                 EXEC SQL
                     CONNECT RESET
                 END-EXEC
                 
                 IF SQLCODE = 0
                     SET WS-DISCONNECTED TO TRUE
                     MOVE 0 TO LS-RETURN-CODE
                 ELSE
                     MOVE SQLCODE TO LS-SQLCODE
                     MOVE 'Error disconnecting from DB2' 
                       TO LS-ERROR-MSG
                     MOVE 8 TO LS-RETURN-CODE
                 END-IF
             END-IF
             .

SI-12/SC-4: retention and access to the SYSOUT/SYSUDUMP output in class X are governed by JES output class and SDSF/RACF JESSPOOL profiles, whose evidence must come from the JES configuration.

##### Limits

The JCL does not show the RACF profiles protecting the PROD.* datasets, the JES class definitions, or whether a scheduler overrides the submitting user.

findings.description:
##### Overview

Operator recovery actions that change job status, return code and restart count are written only to the batch-control record; the only log is a generic ERRPROC message with no process ID, action or user.

##### Applicability

AC-6(9) (log use of privileged functions) and AU-2/AU-3/AU-12 apply: bypassing or terminating a production batch process is a privileged operational function, and the repo's audit service is AUDPROC/AUDITLOG.

##### Evidence

Lines 204-239 REWRITE the control record for restart, bypass and terminate with no AUDPROC call; lines 283-291 send only 'Recovery completed successfully/with errors' to ERRPROC without identifying which processes were changed, the before/after status, or who requested it.

##### Impact

- No record of who bypassed or terminated which job and when; before-images of the status are overwritten.
- Not verified: SMF or scheduler logs outside the repo.
findings.recommendation: Call AUDPROC for each restart/bypass/terminate with type SYST, action UPDATE, the job name/date as key, before and after status/RC images and the requesting user, and treat audit failure as a recovery failure.

findings.title: AUDPROC never sets RETURN-CODE; PORTTRAN cannot detect audit write failure
findings.description:
##### Overview

AUDPROC reports open/write failures only in LS-RETURN-CODE inside the caller's parameter block and via DISPLAY; PORTTRAN tests the RETURN-CODE special register, which AUDPROC never sets, so failed audit writes for portfolio transactions are treated as success.

##### Applicability

AU-5 requires alerting and defined action on audit logging failure; AU-12 requires records to be generated for audited events. AUDPROC is the shared audit writer for PORTTRAN and PORTMSTR.

##### Evidence

AUDPROC lines 62-68 and 86-91 set LS-RETURN-CODE and DISPLAY to SYSOUT; RETURN-CODE is never assigned. PORTTRAN 2310-WRITE-AUDIT-RECORD checks `RETURN-CODE NOT = ZERO` after the CALL. No alert to personnel is raised on failure.

```
AUDFILE open/write fails --> LS-RETURN-CODE=8 + DISPLAY --> PORTTRAN checks RETURN-CODE (0) --> transaction continues unaudited
```

##### Impact

- Portfolio transactions can be applied with no audit record and no alert.
- Not verified: PORTMSTR's post-call check (other batch).
findings.recommendation: Set RETURN-CODE as well as LS-RETURN-CODE on failure (or change callers to test the returned field), make callers stop the transaction on audit failure, and route the failure to an operator alert (e.g. WTO/console message) rather than DISPLAY only.

findings.title: ERRPROC linkage layout mismatches ERR-MESSAGE passed by every caller
findings.description:
##### Overview

All callers in this batch pass ERR-MESSAGE (ERRHAND copybook, beginning with an 18-byte timestamp), but ERRPROC's LS-ERROR-REQUEST begins with an 8-byte program ID, so every error-log record has shifted program, category, code, severity and text fields.

##### Applicability

AU-3 requires event records to establish what, when, where (source) and outcome; ERRPROC writes the system's sequential error log ERRLOG.

##### Evidence

ERRHAND.cpy lines 30-39: ERR-TIMESTAMP X(18), ERR-PROGRAM X(8), ... ERR-DETAILS X(256). ERRPROC lines 38-45: LS-PROGRAM-ID X(8), LS-CATEGORY X(2), LS-ERROR-CODE X(4), LS-SEVERITY COMP, LS-ERROR-TEXT X(80), LS-ERROR-DETAILS X(256), LS-RETURN-CODE. Lines 69-75 copy these into ERR-MESSAGE, so ERR-PROGRAM receives timestamp bytes. Callers include BCHCTL00 line 114, HISTLD00 228, PRCSEQ00 122, RCVPRC00 113/290, DB2CONN 153, DB2CMT 165, DB2ERR 199, DB2STAT 227. Line 69 also moves a 26-byte time into the 18-byte ERR-TIMESTAMP. Log write/open failures (lines 59-62, 88-90) are only DISPLAYed.

##### Impact

- Error-log records misidentify the failing program and corrupt message text across all batch/common modules.
- No user/job identity field exists in the record.
- LS-RETURN-CODE overlays bytes beyond the caller's ERR-MESSAGE.
findings.recommendation: Make ERRPROC's LINKAGE use COPY ERRHAND's ERR-MESSAGE layout (via REPLACING) so caller and callee share one definition, set the timestamp inside ERRPROC with FUNCTION CURRENT-DATE including offset, add a job/user identity field, and return status through a field that exists in the caller's structure.

findings.title: CKPRST checkpoint/restart entry points are empty stubs
findings.description:
##### Overview

CKPRST accepts INIT/TAKE/COMMIT/RESTART requests but every paragraph contains only a comment, so no checkpoint is recorded, verified or restored and RETURN-STATUS is never set. No program in the repo currently CALLs CKPRST, which bounds present exposure.

##### Applicability

SC-24 (fail in a known state preserving state information) and SI-7/SI-7(1) (integrity checks of information) apply to the shared checkpoint/restart service the batch design relies on to resume interrupted jobs without lost or duplicate records.

##### Evidence

Lines 43-57: PROC-INIT, PROC-TAKE-CHECKPOINT, PROC-COMMIT-CHECKPOINT and PROC-RESTART have no statements (the `*` lines in Area B are not valid comment indicators either). The CHECKPOINT-FILE declared at lines 7-12 is never opened, read or written, and RETURN-STATUS is returned unchanged.

##### Impact

- A caller would receive an unchanged status and believe a checkpoint was taken or a restart position restored.
- No integrity check (hash, counts reconciliation) over checkpoint data exists.
- Not verified: whether any JCL or future program depends on CKPRST; no CALL was found in src/programs.
findings.recommendation: Implement the checkpoint record write/read against CKPTFILE with file-status checks, store record counts and a key/position plus an integrity value (e.g. a hash of the checkpointed counters), verify it on RESTART, and set RETURN-STATUS to a failure code on any error so callers stop rather than continue.

findings.title: DB2ERR ERRLOG rows have blank user ID and misaligned timestamp fields
findings.description:
##### Overview

DB2ERR writes SQL error records to the DB2 ERRLOG table with EL-USER-ID forced to spaces and with process date/time sliced from FUNCTION CURRENT-DATE at wrong offsets.

##### Applicability

AU-3 (who/when) and AU-8 (accurate, UTC-mappable timestamps) apply to ERRLOG, the system's database error-event record.

##### Evidence

Line 94 moves SPACES to EL-USER-ID. Lines 90-93: CURRENT-DATE(1:10) yields YYYYMMDDhh, and (12:8) yields minutes/seconds/hundredths plus part of the GMT offset, not a time. Line 75 uses ACCEPT FROM TIME STAMP for EL-ERROR-TIMESTAMP, with no offset.

##### Impact

- Error events cannot be attributed to a user/job and their date/time fields are wrong.
- Not verified: ERRLOG column definitions in the DDL.
findings.recommendation: Populate EL-USER-ID from the job/RACF or CICS user; set EL-PROCESS-DATE from CURRENT-DATE(1:8) and EL-PROCESS-TIME from (9:6); use CURRENT-DATE or DB2 CURRENT TIMESTAMP for the error timestamp and store the offset or UTC.

findings.title: HISTLD00 commits without SQLCODE checks and writes checkpoint after commit
findings.description:
##### Overview

HISTLD00 issues COMMIT WORK at the threshold and at termination without checking SQLCODE, then rewrites the VSAM checkpoint counters as if the commit succeeded; restart logic never reads those counters back.

##### Applicability

SC-24 and SI-7 apply to this batch load of position history into DB2 POSHIST, which must commit DB2 work and record its VSAM checkpoint consistently and fail to a known state.

##### Evidence

Lines 180-187 and 203-207: COMMIT is followed unconditionally by 2310-UPDATE-CHECKPOINT; a failed commit is recorded as progress. Line 130-131: the control record REWRITE has no INVALID KEY/status check. 9000-ERROR-ROUTINE (lines 226-232) rolls back but returns to the processing loop, so after a rollback the in-memory WS-RECORDS-WRITTEN still includes rolled-back rows and the next checkpoint persists them. 1300-INIT-CHECKPOINTS (lines 120-132) never uses BCT-RECORDS-READ to reposition on restart; duplicates on rerun are silently skipped by the SQLCODE -803 CONTINUE at line 168-169.

```
COMMIT (rc unchecked) --> REWRITE checkpoint counts --> restart ignores counts
```

##### Impact

- Batch control counts can overstate what was durably loaded into POSHIST, losing reliable state information for recovery.
- -803 suppression masks reprocessing but also masks genuine key collisions.
- Not verified: DB2-ERROR-ROUTINE in DBPROC behaviour beyond its ROLLBACK/ERRPROC call.
findings.recommendation: Test SQLCODE after each COMMIT and terminate (with ROLLBACK and a non-zero RC) on failure; only rewrite the checkpoint after a successful commit and check its file status; reset counters to the last committed values on rollback; on restart, read BCT-RECORDS-READ and skip that many input records; count -803 occurrences separately and report them.

                 MOVE 0 TO WS-COMMIT-COUNT
                 
                 PERFORM 2310-UPDATE-CHECKPOINT
             END-IF
             .

             MOVE WS-RECORDS-READ TO BCT-RECORDS-READ
             MOVE WS-RECORDS-WRITTEN TO BCT-RECORDS-WRITTEN
             
             REWRITE BATCH-CONTROL-RECORD
                 INVALID KEY
                     MOVE 'Error updating checkpoint' TO ERR-TEXT
                     PERFORM 9000-ERROR-ROUTINE
             END-REWRITE
             .
             
         3100-FINAL-COMMIT.
             EXEC SQL

             END-EXEC

findings.title: AUDPROC timestamps from ACCEPT TIME STAMP and caller-supplied user ID
findings.description:
##### Overview

Audit timestamps come from `ACCEPT ... FROM TIME STAMP`, which is not a standard Enterprise COBOL ACCEPT source and carries no UTC offset, and the user identity is whatever the caller passes rather than the authenticated identity.

##### Applicability

AU-8 (system-clock timestamps mappable to UTC) and AU-3/AU-10 (records establish, irrefutably, who performed the action) apply to the central audit writer.

##### Evidence

Line 60 obtains WS-FORMATTED-TIME by ACCEPT FROM TIME STAMP; FUNCTION CURRENT-DATE (date, time and GMT offset) is not used. Lines 37 and 75 take LS-USER-ID from the caller's parameter block; nothing obtains the user from CICS ASSIGN USERID or the RACF ACEE.

##### Impact

- Audit times cannot be reliably mapped to UTC; a caller can record any user ID.
- Not verified: compiler behaviour for ACCEPT FROM TIME STAMP.
findings.recommendation: Use FUNCTION CURRENT-DATE (or DB2 CURRENT TIMESTAMP - CURRENT TIMEZONE) and store the offset/UTC; derive the user ID inside AUDPROC from the security environment (CICS ASSIGN USERID online, RACF ACEE/job user in batch) instead of trusting the caller.

findings.description:
##### Overview

##### Applicability

SI-10 applies to the recovery request parameters (process date, recovery type, process ID) that select which control records are rewritten.

##### Evidence

##### Impact

- An invalid request can still rewrite control records.
- Not verified: caller behaviour on the INIT return code.
findings.recommendation: GOBACK with the error code from 9000 during INIT, keep a validated flag that RECV requires, and validate LS-PROCESS-DATE as a real CCYYMMDD date.

findings.title: DB2CMT passes LS-ERROR-INFO to DB2ERR, so commit/rollback failures go unlogged
findings.description:
##### Overview

On commit, rollback or savepoint failure DB2CMT calls DB2ERR with only the SQLCODE/message area, but DB2ERR expects a request beginning with a 4-byte function code; the SQLCODE bytes are read as the function, DB2ERR falls to 'Invalid function code', and no ERRLOG row is written. Rollback failure is returned as RC 8 without failing closed. No program currently CALLs DB2CMT.

##### Applicability

SC-24 (fail to a known state) and AU-12/AU-5 (generate records and respond to logging failures) apply to the shared DB2 commit controller.

##### Evidence

Line 169 `CALL 'DB2ERR' USING LS-ERROR-INFO` passes the 84-byte area defined at lines 48-50; DB2ERR's LS-ERROR-REQUEST (DB2ERR lines 39-53) starts with LS-FUNCTION X(4) and LS-PROGRAM-ID, so FUNC-LOG never matches. Lines 103-117: rollback failure only sets RC 8.

##### Impact

- DB2 commit/rollback failures leave no ERRLOG record with SQLCODE/SQLSTATE.
- A failed rollback leaves the unit of work in an undefined state while the caller may continue.
findings.recommendation: Build a DB2ERR request (function 'LOG ', program 'DB2CMT', SQLCODE, SQLSTATE, text) and pass it; on rollback failure return a terminal code (16) and document that callers must abend.

snippets.commentary: Commit and rollback failure paths.
snippets.code:
2100-ISSUE-COMMIT.
             EXEC SQL
                 COMMIT WORK
             END-EXEC
             
             IF SQLCODE = 0
                 ADD 1 TO WS-COMMIT-COUNT
                 MOVE 0 TO LS-RETURN-CODE
             ELSE
                 MOVE SQLCODE TO LS-SQLCODE
                 MOVE 'Commit failed' TO LS-ERROR-MSG
                 MOVE 8 TO LS-RETURN-CODE
                 PERFORM 9100-LOG-ERROR
             END-IF
             .
             
         3000-ROLLBACK.
             EXEC SQL
                 ROLLBACK WORK
             END-EXEC
             
             IF SQLCODE = 0
                 ADD 1 TO WS-ROLLBACK-COUNT
                 MOVE 0 TO LS-RETURN-CODE
             ELSE
                 MOVE SQLCODE TO LS-SQLCODE
                 MOVE 'Rollback failed' TO LS-ERROR-MSG
                 MOVE 8 TO LS-RETURN-CODE
                 PERFORM 9100-LOG-ERROR
             END-IF
             .

findings.title: SECMGR user validation compares caller-supplied ID to same CICS USERID
findings.description:
##### Overview
P100-VALIDATE-USER only checks that the user ID in the COMMAREA equals the ID returned by EXEC CICS ASSIGN USERID. The only caller in the repo, INQONLN, fills that COMMAREA field from the same ASSIGN USERID, so the check always passes. SECMGR adds no authentication of its own: no ESM/RACF verification, no counter of failed attempts, no lockout. Whether CICS sign-on is enforced by the region's ESM is runtime configuration outside the repo.

##### Applicability
IA-2 covers identifying and authenticating organizational users. AC-7 covers limiting consecutive invalid logon attempts and the action taken when the limit is hit. SECMGR is the documented security manager for online programs (lines 4-8), so this is where application-level validation and attempt limiting would sit. Sign-on done by CICS/RACF before the transaction starts is out of scope for this repo and must be evidenced from the region's SIT/ESM settings.

##### Evidence
- SECMGR.cbl:56-74 compares `SEC-USER-ID` to `WS-USER-ID`, both taken from ASSIGN USERID.
- INQONLN.cbl:142-144 sets `SEC-USER-ID` from ASSIGN USERID right before the LINK.
- So the comparison is tautological. A failure (code 8) cannot happen through the in-repo caller, and no failed-attempt state is kept or checked anywhere.

##### Impact
- The 'Validates CICS user credentials' function documented in the header does no credential validation. Identity rests entirely on whatever the region provides, which could be the default CICS user if sign-on is not enforced.
- No [number] of invalid attempts and no lock action is implemented in the application.
- Not verified: CICS SEC=YES / RACF sign-on settings and the default-user configuration of the region.
findings.recommendation: Replace the tautological comparison with a real ESM-backed check: EXEC CICS VERIFY PASSWORD/QUERY SECURITY, or rely on CICS sign-on and reject the region default user ID. Persist failed validation and authorization attempts per user and lock or deny after an organization-defined threshold.

snippets.commentary: Validation is only an equality check between the COMMAREA user ID and ASSIGN USERID; there is no ESM call and no attempt counter.
snippets.code:
P100-VALIDATE-USER.
             EXEC CICS ASSIGN
                       USERID(WS-USER-ID)
                       RESP(SEC-RESPONSE-CODE)
             END-EXEC.
             
             IF SEC-RESPONSE-CODE = DFHRESP(NORMAL)
                IF SEC-USER-ID = WS-USER-ID
                   MOVE 0 TO SEC-RESPONSE-CODE
                ELSE
                   MOVE 'User validation failed' 
                     TO SEC-ERROR-INFO
                   MOVE 8 TO SEC-RESPONSE-CODE
                END-IF
             ELSE
                MOVE 'Unable to obtain user credentials' 
                  TO SEC-ERROR-INFO
                MOVE 12 TO SEC-RESPONSE-CODE
             END-IF.

snippets.commentary: The caller fills SEC-USER-ID from the same ASSIGN USERID before linking to SECMGR, so the comparison always matches.
snippets.code:

             MOVE 'V' TO SEC-REQUEST-TYPE.

                       USERID(SEC-USER-ID)
             END-EXEC.

                       COMMAREA(WS-SECURITY-REQUEST)
                       LENGTH(LENGTH OF WS-SECURITY-REQUEST)
             END-EXEC.

findings.description:
##### Overview
When AUDPROC returns non-zero, PORTTRAN routes the error to ERRPROC, increments the error count and continues with the next transaction. The REWRITE has already happened. The run stops only after more than 100 errors. As with the finding above, this path is currently unreachable because 2200 is not PERFORMed.

##### Applicability
AU-5 requires alerting and defined actions on audit logging failure.

##### Evidence
- PORTTRAN.cbl:292-300 calls AUDPROC and, on a non-zero RETURN-CODE, PERFORMs 9000.
- PORTTRAN.cbl:311-317 only logs through ERRPROC.
- PORTTRAN.cbl:66 allows up to 100 errors.

##### Impact
- Holdings changes can go unaudited with no stop and no specific alert.
- Not verified: whether ERRPROC raises an alert for this category.
findings.recommendation: Treat an AUDPROC failure as fatal: set a non-zero RC, stop posting, and alert operations. Alternatively, back out the REWRITE so that no update persists without its audit record.

findings.description:
##### Overview
When the AUDITLOG insert fails, P300 only moves 'Audit logging failed' and response code 12 into the COMMAREA. No operator message, alert or other action is raised. In the in-repo caller (INQONLN), the transaction has already been authorized by the time the 'L' call is made.

AU-5 requires alerting defined personnel or roles when audit logging fails, and taking defined additional actions. SECMGR owns the online security audit write.

##### Evidence
- SECMGR.cbl:127-133 sets code 12 and text on a non-zero SQLCODE. Nothing is written to a console, TD queue or alerting path.
- INQONLN.cbl:161-168 makes the 'L' call last and does not test its response code inside P050.

##### Impact
- Online access can continue silently while no security audit records are being written.
- Not verified: whether INQONLN checks SEC-RESPONSE-CODE after P050 returns (that file belongs to another batch), and whether DB2 or CICS monitoring alerts on the SQL error.
findings.recommendation: On audit insert failure, write an alert to a monitored destination (e.g. EXEC CICS WRITE OPERATOR or a TD queue routed to security operations). Make callers treat code 12 from 'L' as a hard stop, or abend the task, according to the organization-defined AU-5 action.

findings.title: SECMGR audit omits outcome and never records denied validation or authorization
findings.description:
##### Overview
SECMGR writes AUDITLOG rows only when asked with request type 'L'. INQONLN asks for that only after validation and authorization both succeed. Neither P100 nor P200 writes a record when it denies access, and the AUDITLOG insert has no outcome or status column.

##### Applicability
AU-2 and AU-12 cover generating records for the defined security event types, which include logon and access-denial events. AU-3 requires records to show the outcome of the event. AC-2(12) monitoring of atypical usage depends on failed attempts being recorded. SECMGR is the component documented as maintaining the security audit trail (line 8).

##### Evidence
- SECMGR.cbl:62-74 and 88-101 set failure codes and messages, but no audit write follows.
- SECMGR.cbl:117-125 inserts timestamp, user, terminal, transaction, program and access type, with no outcome field.
- INQONLN.cbl:161-168 links with 'L' only inside the success branches.

```
P100/P200 failure --code 8/12--> caller --no 'L' request--> no AUDITLOG row
```

##### Impact
- Failed and denied access attempts leave no application audit trail, so atypical usage and brute-force attempts cannot be detected from AUDITLOG.
- Successful records do not state their outcome explicitly. It can only be inferred from the fact that a row exists.
- Not verified: whether CICS/RACF SMF records capture these denials at the platform level.
findings.recommendation: Have P100 and P200 call P300 (or an equivalent insert) on every outcome, and add an OUTCOME/STATUS column plus the reason code to the AUDITLOG insert, so that granted, denied and failed events are all recorded.
findings.note: Root cause for online access-audit gaps (AU-2/AU-3/AU-12/AU-8): SECMGR P300 is the only AUDITLOG writer and is only invoked on success; insert has no outcome/object column and uses FUNCTION CURRENT-DATE for the timestamp. One fix in SECMGR (write a record from P100/P200 on deny with outcome + account number, use CURRENT TIMESTAMP) also resolves INQONLN denial-audit member sfind-e55c6680f9844fbc92bd3a4cd21e2f22. Merged duplicates: sfind-7d5cf59a27a742f5a47625c17477377c, sfind-e98eea4b311a4925abc132422f575797, sfind-4a5c55fb42b3487882bf6a3dbf116f35.

                         MOVE 8 TO SEC-RESPONSE-CODE
                      END-IF
                 WHEN OTHER

                        TO SEC-ERROR-INFO

findings.title: PORTADD creates portfolio master records with no audit record
findings.description:
##### Overview
PORTADD writes new records to the portfolio master VSAM file and produces only count totals on SYSOUT. It does not call AUDPROC, does not write an audit file, and does not set PORT-LAST-USER, so nothing records who created which portfolio or when.

##### Applicability
AU-2 and AU-12 cover generating audit records for defined events, and record creation in the system of record is one of them. AU-3 covers the identity, outcome and object content of those records. The repo provides AUDPROC and the AUDITLOG copybook for this purpose, and sibling programs (PORTDEL, PORTTRAN) use them.

##### Evidence
- PORTADD.cbl:113-137 validates, sets the create and maintenance dates, and issues WRITE PORT-RECORD. Successes, duplicates and errors only increment counters or DISPLAY the ID.
- No AUDIT file is selected (lines 20-31), and there is no CALL 'AUDPROC' anywhere in the program.
- PORT-LAST-USER (PORTFLIO.cpy line 32) is never populated.

##### Impact
- Creation of client portfolio records (account number, client name, financial data) cannot be traced to an individual or a job run.
- Assumption: the JCL job log and SMF are not treated as the application audit trail. SMF job records would show the submitter but not which records were created.
findings.recommendation: After each WRITE attempt, populate an AUDITLOG AUDIT-RECORD (user ID, program, action CREATE, SUCC/FAIL status, portfolio ID and account number, after-image) and CALL 'AUDPROC'. Set PORT-LAST-USER before the WRITE. Stop or flag the run if AUDPROC returns non-zero.

findings.title: PORTVALD portfolio ID, account, type and amount validation subroutine
findings.description:
##### Artifact
PORTVALD.cbl:31-120 is a called subroutine with four checks. The portfolio ID must start with 'PORT' and have numeric positions 5-8. The account value must be NUMERIC and not zeros; this test runs on the full 50-byte LS-INPUT-VALUE. The investment type must be STK, BND, MMF or ETF. The amount is moved from the X(50) input into S9(13)V99 and range-checked against ±9999999999999.99, with no prior NUMERIC test. An unknown request type returns VAL-INVALID-ID. Error text comes from fixed messages in the PORTVAL copybook.

##### Bears on
SI-10 (input validation rules available to callers) and SI-11 (generic error messages).

##### Limits
This does not show which programs call PORTVALD. PORTADD and PORTTRAN in this batch do not.

snippets.commentary: Validation dispatcher and the four validation rules.
snippets.code:
PROCEDURE DIVISION USING LS-VALIDATION-REQUEST.
         0000-MAIN.
             INITIALIZE VAL-WORK-AREAS
             
             EVALUATE TRUE
                 WHEN LS-VAL-ID
                     PERFORM 1000-VALIDATE-ID
                 WHEN LS-VAL-ACCT
                     PERFORM 2000-VALIDATE-ACCOUNT
                 WHEN LS-VAL-TYPE
                     PERFORM 3000-VALIDATE-TYPE
                 WHEN LS-VAL-AMT
                     PERFORM 4000-VALIDATE-AMOUNT
                 WHEN OTHER
                     MOVE VAL-INVALID-ID TO LS-RETURN-CODE
                     MOVE 'Invalid validation type' TO LS-ERROR-MSG
             END-EVALUATE
             
             GOBACK
             .
             
         1000-VALIDATE-ID.
        *----------------------------------------------------------------*
        * Portfolio ID must start with 'PORT' and have 4 numeric digits
        *----------------------------------------------------------------*
             IF LS-INPUT-VALUE(1:4) NOT = VAL-ID-PREFIX
                 MOVE VAL-INVALID-ID TO LS-RETURN-CODE
                 MOVE VAL-ERR-ID TO LS-ERROR-MSG
                 EXIT PARAGRAPH
             END-IF
             
             MOVE LS-INPUT-VALUE(5:4) TO VAL-NUMERIC-CHECK
             IF VAL-NUMERIC-CHECK IS NOT NUMERIC
                 MOVE VAL-INVALID-ID TO LS-RETURN-CODE
                 MOVE VAL-ERR-ID TO LS-ERROR-MSG
                 EXIT PARAGRAPH
             END-IF
             
             MOVE VAL-SUCCESS TO LS-RETURN-CODE
             MOVE SPACES TO LS-ERROR-MSG
             .
             
         2000-VALIDATE-ACCOUNT.
        *----------------------------------------------------------------*
        * Account number must be 10 numeric digits
        *----------------------------------------------------------------*
             IF LS-INPUT-VALUE IS NOT NUMERIC
             OR LS-INPUT-VALUE = ZEROS
                 MOVE VAL-INVALID-ACCT TO LS-RETURN-CODE
                 MOVE VAL-ERR-ACCT TO LS-ERROR-MSG
                 EXIT PARAGRAPH
             END-IF
             
             MOVE VAL-SUCCESS TO LS-RETURN-CODE
             MOVE SPACES TO LS-ERROR-MSG
             .
             
         3000-VALIDATE-TYPE.
        *----------------------------------------------------------------*
        * Investment type must be valid value
        *----------------------------------------------------------------*
             IF LS-INPUT-VALUE NOT = 'STK'
                AND NOT = 'BND'
                AND NOT = 'MMF'
                AND NOT = 'ETF'
                 MOVE VAL-INVALID-TYPE TO LS-RETURN-CODE
                 MOVE VAL-ERR-TYPE TO LS-ERROR-MSG
                 EXIT PARAGRAPH
             END-IF
             
             MOVE VAL-SUCCESS TO LS-RETURN-CODE
             MOVE SPACES TO LS-ERROR-MSG
             .
             
         4000-VALIDATE-AMOUNT.
        *----------------------------------------------------------------*
        * Amount must be within valid range
        *----------------------------------------------------------------*
             MOVE LS-INPUT-VALUE TO VAL-TEMP-NUM
             
             IF VAL-TEMP-NUM < VAL-MIN-AMOUNT
             OR VAL-TEMP-NUM > VAL-MAX-AMOUNT
                 MOVE VAL-INVALID-AMT TO LS-RETURN-CODE
                 MOVE VAL-ERR-AMT TO LS-ERROR-MSG
                 EXIT PARAGRAPH
             END-IF
             
             MOVE VAL-SUCCESS TO LS-RETURN-CODE
             MOVE SPACES TO LS-ERROR-MSG
             .

##### Artifact
SECMGR.cbl:78-103 (P200-CHECK-AUTH) counts rows in table AUTHFILE that match USER_ID, RESOURCE and ACCESS_TYPE, and returns 0 (granted) or 8 ('Access denied'). AUTHFILE is not defined anywhere in the repository's DDL. The only resource and access type requested in the repo is INQONLN/READ.

findings.title: PORTDEL audit timestamp from non-standard ACCEPT FROM TIME STAMP
findings.description:
##### Overview
The deletion audit timestamp comes from `ACCEPT ... FROM TIME STAMP`. That is not a standard or IBM Enterprise COBOL ACCEPT source, so the value's format, and whether it carries any UTC offset, is undefined in the code.

##### Applicability
AU-8 requires audit timestamps generated from the system clock in UTC, or with a fixed offset or mapping, at a defined granularity. AUD-TIMESTAMP is the only time field in the PORTDEL audit record.

##### Evidence
- PORTDEL.cbl:169-171 accepts into WS-TIMESTAMP and moves it to AUD-TIMESTAMP. By contrast, SECMGR and PORTTRAN use FUNCTION CURRENT-DATE, which includes the GMT offset.

##### Impact
- Deletion audit records may have no timestamp that can be interpreted or correlated with other records. Behavior depends on the compiler: it may be rejected at compile time or yield local time with no zone.
- Not verified: the compiler and runtime behavior.
findings.recommendation: Use MOVE FUNCTION CURRENT-DATE TO WS-TIMESTAMP (21 characters including the GMT offset), or a DB2 CURRENT TIMESTAMP with an explicit UTC conversion, and document the format.

snippets.commentary: The audit timestamp source is ACCEPT FROM TIME STAMP.
snippets.code:

             ACCEPT WS-TIMESTAMP FROM TIME STAMP
             
             MOVE WS-TIMESTAMP TO AUD-TIMESTAMP

##### Overview
PORTREAD reads the entire portfolio master and DISPLAYs each record's ID, account number, client name, status and total value. The JCL routes SYSOUT to the job's output class (SYSOUT=*, MSGCLASS=X). How that spool output is protected and retained is controlled outside the repo.

##### Applicability
SI-12 requires that information output from the system is handled and retained according to policy. The account number and client name are client-identifying financial data. The output here goes to an unmasked spool listing, not to a controlled report dataset.

##### Evidence
- PORTREAD.cbl:95-103 DISPLAYs PORT-ACCOUNT-NO and PORT-CLIENT-NAME, unmasked, for every record.
- PORTREAD.jcl:13 sends SYSOUT to the default spool class.

```
PORTFOLIO.MASTER.FILE --READ NEXT--> DISPLAY --> JES spool (MSGCLASS=X), unmasked
```

##### Impact
- The full client account and name list ends up in job output that anyone with spool access for that class can view, under whatever JES purge policy applies.
- Not verified: JES spool security (RACF JESSPOOL class) and the retention period for class X.
findings.recommendation: Mask the account number (e.g. show only the last 4 digits) and omit the client name from DISPLAY output. If a full listing is required, write it to a protected report dataset with a defined retention.

findings.title: SECMGR authorization can fail open on unknown request type and SQLCA-bound COUNT
findings.description:
##### Overview
SECMGR's access decision has two fail-open paths. First, the request-type EVALUATE has no WHEN OTHER, so an unrecognized request type returns without setting SEC-RESPONSE-CODE and the caller's previous value (0 after a successful call) is left in place. Second, the P200 COUNT(*) is selected INTO WS-DB2-AREA, which is the group holding the SQLCA, rather than a numeric host variable. The `> 0` test therefore compares the SQLCA bytes, not a count. How the precompiler or runtime handles the second path was not verified.

##### Applicability
AC-3 requires that approved authorizations are enforced for logical access. SC-24 requires failing to a known state. SECMGR's P200 is the application's authorization enforcement point for online resources.

##### Evidence
- SECMGR.cbl:42-52 dispatches only on 'V', 'A' and 'L', with no default branch that sets a denial code.
- SECMGR.cbl:15-16 makes WS-DB2-AREA the SQLCA include group.
- SECMGR.cbl:79-96 uses WS-DB2-AREA as the INTO target and the comparison operand. If the decision is made on SQLCA bytes such as the 'SQLCA' eyecatcher, the result is not driven by the AUTHFILE row count.

##### Impact
- Access to online resources could be granted with no matching AUTHFILE entry.
- Assumption: the code compiles as written. If the precompiler rejects line 81, P200 is not deployable at all.
- Runtime verification is needed: call P200 for a user with no AUTHFILE row and check the response code.
findings.recommendation: Add WHEN OTHER that sets a denial code (e.g. 8 with 'Invalid security request'), and initialize SEC-RESPONSE-CODE to a non-zero value on entry. Select COUNT(*) into a dedicated PIC S9(9) COMP host variable and grant only when SQLCODE = 0 and that count > 0.

snippets.commentary: There is no WHEN OTHER, so an unknown request type returns with SEC-RESPONSE-CODE unchanged.
snippets.code:
EVALUATE TRUE
                 WHEN SEC-VALIDATE
                      PERFORM P100-VALIDATE-USER
                         THRU P100-EXIT
                 WHEN SEC-AUTHORIZE
                      PERFORM P200-CHECK-AUTH
                         THRU P200-EXIT
                 WHEN SEC-AUDIT
                      PERFORM P300-LOG-ACCESS
                         THRU P300-EXIT
             END-EVALUATE.
             
             EXEC CICS RETURN END-EXEC.

snippets.commentary: WS-DB2-AREA is the group containing the SQLCA.
snippets.code:
01  WS-DB2-AREA.
             EXEC SQL INCLUDE SQLCA END-EXEC.

snippets.commentary: The COUNT is selected into, and compared from, the SQLCA group instead of a dedicated numeric host variable.
snippets.code:
EXEC SQL
                  SELECT COUNT(*)
                  INTO :WS-DB2-AREA
                  FROM AUTHFILE
                  WHERE USER_ID = :SEC-USER-ID
                    AND RESOURCE = :SEC-RESOURCE-NAME
                    AND ACCESS_TYPE = :SEC-ACCESS-TYPE
             END-EXEC.
             
             EVALUATE SQLCODE
                 WHEN 0
                      IF WS-DB2-AREA > 0
                         MOVE 0 TO SEC-RESPONSE-CODE
                      ELSE
                         MOVE 'Access denied' 
                           TO SEC-ERROR-INFO
                         MOVE 8 TO SEC-RESPONSE-CODE
                      END-IF

findings.title: PORTDEL deletion audit record lacks user identity and deleted content
findings.description:
##### Overview
PORTDEL writes an audit record for each successful VSAM DELETE. The record holds only a timestamp, the action, the key, the reason code and the status byte. There is no user or job identity, no program name, and no image of the deleted record. Failed deletes and not-found requests are not audited at all.

##### Applicability
AU-3 requires records to establish the identity of the individual or process, and the outcome. AU-10 relates to proving who performed a deletion. Deleting client portfolio master records is a security-relevant event that falls under AU-12.

##### Evidence
- PORTDEL.cbl:56-62 defines AUDIT-RECORD with no user, program or before-image field. 27 bytes are FILLER.
- PORTDEL.cbl:168-177 fills only those fields.
- PORTDEL.cbl:146-165 has the not-found and failed-delete paths, which only DISPLAY.

##### Impact
- A deleted portfolio, including client name and balances, cannot be reconstructed from the audit trail, and the deletion cannot be attributed to a person.
- Only successful deletes appear in the trail. Failed or unauthorized attempts are visible only on SYSOUT.
findings.recommendation: Switch to the shared AUDITLOG copybook and AUDPROC. Record the user/job ID, the program, action DELETE, SUCC/FAIL, the portfolio ID and account, and the record image as it was before deletion. Audit failed and not-found delete requests as well.

snippets.commentary: The local audit layout has no identity, program or before-image fields.
snippets.code:
01  AUDIT-RECORD.
             05  AUD-TIMESTAMP      PIC X(26).
             05  AUD-ACTION         PIC X(6).
             05  AUD-KEY           PIC X(18).
             05  AUD-REASON        PIC X(2).
             05  AUD-STATUS        PIC X(1).
             05  AUD-FILLER        PIC X(27).

snippets.commentary: Audit population covers only timestamp, action, key, reason and status.

2300-WRITE-AUDIT.
             ACCEPT WS-TIMESTAMP FROM TIME STAMP
             
             MOVE WS-TIMESTAMP TO AUD-TIMESTAMP
             MOVE 'DELETE' TO AUD-ACTION
             MOVE PORT-KEY TO AUD-KEY
             MOVE DEL-REASON-CODE TO AUD-REASON
             MOVE PORT-STATUS TO AUD-STATUS
             
             WRITE AUDIT-RECORD
             
             IF NOT WS-AUD-SUCCESS
                 DISPLAY 'Audit write failed for: ' PORT-KEY
             END-IF
             .

             MOVE DEL-KEY TO PORT-KEY
             
             READ PORTFOLIO-FILE
             
             EVALUATE TRUE
                 WHEN WS-SUCCESS-STATUS
                     PERFORM 2200-DELETE-RECORD
                 WHEN WS-REC-NOT-FND
                     ADD 1 TO WS-NOT-FND-COUNT
                     DISPLAY 'Record not found: ' PORT-KEY
                 WHEN OTHER
                     ADD 1 TO WS-ERROR-COUNT
                     DISPLAY 'Read error for: ' PORT-KEY
             END-EVALUATE
             .
             
         2200-DELETE-RECORD.
             DELETE PORTFOLIO-FILE
