findings.title: PORTDEL audit write failure only DISPLAYs; deletion already committed
findings.description:
##### Overview
PORTDEL deletes the master record first and writes the audit record afterwards. If the audit WRITE fails, the program DISPLAYs a message and moves on to the next deletion with the return code unchanged, so the job can end RC=0 having deleted records that were never audited.

##### Applicability
AU-5 requires alerting and defined actions when audit logging fails. PORTDEL's audit file is the only record of portfolio deletions.

##### Evidence
- PORTDEL.cbl:157-166 performs DELETE and then PERFORM 2300-WRITE-AUDIT.
- PORTDEL.cbl:179-181 only DISPLAYs on a non-'00' audit status, and WS-RETURN-CODE is not set.

##### Impact
- Portfolio deletions can be lost from the audit trail without anyone being alerted or the job failing.
- Not verified: whether operations monitor SYSOUT for this message.
findings.recommendation: On audit write failure, set a non-zero return code, stop processing further deletions, and issue an operator/console alert. Where possible, write the audit record before committing the delete, or roll back the delete.

snippets.commentary: The delete happens before the audit write.
snippets.code:
2200-DELETE-RECORD.
             DELETE PORTFOLIO-FILE
             
             IF WS-SUCCESS-STATUS
                 ADD 1 TO WS-DELETE-COUNT
                 PERFORM 2300-WRITE-AUDIT
             ELSE
                 ADD 1 TO WS-ERROR-COUNT
                 DISPLAY 'Delete failed for: ' PORT-KEY
             END-IF
             .

snippets.commentary: An audit write failure is only displayed; processing and RC are unaffected.

             IF NOT WS-AUD-SUCCESS
                 DISPLAY 'Audit write failed for: ' PORT-KEY
             END-IF

findings.title: PORTTRAN audit before-image captured after update, after-image never set
findings.description:
##### Overview
In PORTTRAN, 2300-UPDATE-AUDIT-TRAIL runs after the REWRITE. It copies the already-updated record into AUD-BEFORE-IMAGE, never sets AUD-AFTER-IMAGE, maps a SELL to action 'DELETE', and derives SUCC/FAIL from the last file status rather than the outcome of the update. The update and audit paragraph (2200) is not currently PERFORMed from 2100, so this applies when the posting path is wired in.

##### Applicability
AU-3 requires audit records to establish what type of event occurred and its outcome. AU-3(1) covers additional content such as before and after values. PORTTRAN is the transaction-posting program that changes holdings in the portfolio master.

##### Evidence
- PORTTRAN.cbl:167-180 REWRITEs inside 2210/2220/2240 and only then PERFORMs 2300.
- PORTTRAN.cbl:278 moves PORT-RECORD, the post-update state, into the before-image, and no after-image is set.
- PORTTRAN.cbl:257-266 maps SL to 'DELETE' and TR to 'UPDATE' even though TR is not implemented.
- PORTTRAN.cbl:268-272 bases the status on WS-PORT-STATUS.
- PORTTRAN.cbl:102-118 never PERFORMs 2200-UPDATE-POSITIONS.

##### Impact
- Records cannot show the original holdings. Sells look like deletions. Failed transfers can be recorded with 'SUCC' if the last file status was '00'.
- Assumption: 2200 will be invoked in production. Today the mutation path is unreachable, so the program neither changes nor audits holdings.
- Not verified: PORTREC copybook layout (not in repo) and the behavior of `FUNCTION USER-ID` (not an IBM intrinsic function).
findings.recommendation: Save the record image into AUD-BEFORE-IMAGE before applying the update and the post-REWRITE image into AUD-AFTER-IMAGE. Map BU/SL/FE to UPDATE with the transaction type in the message. Set SUCC/FAIL from the outcome of the specific REWRITE. Use a supported user-identity source, e.g. from the job or ACEE via an assembler stub or CICS ASSIGN.

2200-UPDATE-POSITIONS.
             EVALUATE TRN-TYPE
                 WHEN 'BU'
                     PERFORM 2210-PROCESS-BUY
                 WHEN 'SL'
                     PERFORM 2220-PROCESS-SELL
                 WHEN 'TR'
                     PERFORM 2230-PROCESS-TRANSFER
                 WHEN 'FE'
                     PERFORM 2240-PROCESS-FEE
             END-EVALUATE
             
             PERFORM 2300-UPDATE-AUDIT-TRAIL
             .

             MOVE 'PORTTRAN'     TO AUD-PROGRAM
             MOVE FUNCTION USER-ID TO AUD-USER-ID
             MOVE 'TRAN'         TO AUD-TYPE

                 WHEN 'BU'
                     MOVE 'CREATE  ' TO AUD-ACTION
                 WHEN 'SL'
                     MOVE 'DELETE  ' TO AUD-ACTION
                 WHEN 'TR'
                     MOVE 'UPDATE  ' TO AUD-ACTION
                 WHEN 'FE'

             END-EVALUATE

             END-IF

                    TRN-AMOUNT     DELIMITED BY SIZE
                    ' Units: '     DELIMITED BY SIZE

findings.title: DB2ONLN CONNECT TO POSMVP without user credentials
findings.description:
##### Artifact
Line 67 issues `EXEC SQL CONNECT TO POSMVP` with no USER/USING clause; no credential literals exist in the program. The PINQ DB2ENTRY in src/cics/PORTDFN.csd (lines 82-88) specifies AUTHTYPE(USERID). On SQL errors (lines 77, 99) SQLERRMC is copied into DB2-ERROR-MSG returned to the caller, and P300 returns CURRENT SERVER in the same field.

##### Bears on
IA-5 / IA-5(6) / IA-2: the DB2 authorization identity is handed to the CICS-DB2 attach (thread authorization by signed-on user ID); evidence of how that identity is authenticated and authorized must come from the CICS DB2CONN/DB2ENTRY runtime definitions and DB2/RACF grants. SI-11: the SQLERRMC text is passed back to calling programs.

##### Limits
Does not show whether the calling programs display DB2-ERROR-MSG to terminal users; in this batch DB2RECV and INQHIST do not copy it to the screen.

snippets.commentary: Credential-less CONNECT and SQLERRMC/CURRENT SERVER returned in DB2-ERROR-MSG.
snippets.code:
P110-ESTABLISH-CONNECTION.
             EXEC SQL CONNECT TO POSMVP END-EXEC.
             
             IF SQLCODE = 0
                ADD 1 TO WS-ACTIVE-CONNECTIONS
                MOVE SQLCODE TO DB2-SQLCODE
                MOVE 0 TO DB2-RESPONSE-CODE
                PERFORM P120-GENERATE-TOKEN
                   THRU P120-EXIT
             ELSE
                MOVE SQLCODE TO DB2-SQLCODE
                MOVE SQLERRMC TO DB2-ERROR-MSG
                MOVE -1 TO DB2-RESPONSE-CODE
             END-IF.
         P110-EXIT.
             EXIT.
             
         P120-GENERATE-TOKEN.
             MOVE FUNCTION CURRENT-DATE TO DB2-CONNECTION-TOKEN.
             STRING DB2-CONNECTION-TOKEN DELIMITED BY SIZE
                    WS-ACTIVE-CONNECTIONS DELIMITED BY SIZE
                    INTO DB2-CONNECTION-TOKEN.
         P120-EXIT.
             EXIT.
             
         P200-PROCESS-DISCONNECT.
             EXEC SQL DISCONNECT END-EXEC.
             
             IF SQLCODE = 0
                SUBTRACT 1 FROM WS-ACTIVE-CONNECTIONS
                MOVE 0 TO DB2-RESPONSE-CODE
             ELSE
                MOVE SQLCODE TO DB2-SQLCODE
                MOVE SQLERRMC TO DB2-ERROR-MSG
                MOVE -1 TO DB2-RESPONSE-CODE
             END-IF.
         P200-EXIT.
             EXIT.
             
         P300-CHECK-STATUS.
             EXEC SQL SELECT CURRENT SERVER 
                      INTO :DB2-ERROR-MSG
             END-EXEC.

##### Artifact
The template connects with `CONNECT TO sample` (lines 79-81) with no credentials. 9000-CHECK-SQL-STATUS (lines 222-237) DISPLAYs SQLCODE and SQLERRMC to SYSOUT on any non-zero SQLCODE, and for negative codes performs ROLLBACK WORK, sets RETURN-CODE 8 and runs 3000-TERMINATE (COMMIT WORK, CONNECT RESET, lines 209-220). ##### Limits
Template only; does not show which production programs follow it or who can read SYSOUT.

findings.title: SECMGR authorizes a caller-supplied user ID against an application table
findings.description:
##### Overview
SECMGR P200 decides access by counting AUTHFILE rows for SEC-USER-ID taken from the caller's COMMAREA, not the CICS-signed-on user, and the COUNT result is selected into the SQLCA group rather than a numeric host variable, so the access test at line 90 does not reliably evaluate the count. No ESM (RACF QUERY SECURITY) call is made. AUTHFILE has no DDL in the repo.

##### Applicability
AC-3 (enforce approved authorizations) and AC-6 (least privilege): SECMGR is the repo's central online access-enforcement function. Any program that can LINK SECMGR controls the identity being authorized.

##### Evidence
Lines 79-86 use `:SEC-USER-ID` (linkage, line 35) in the WHERE clause; the trusted ASSIGN USERID is obtained only in P100/P300. Line 81 selects INTO `:WS-DB2-AREA`, which is the SQLCA include group (lines 15-16), and line 90 compares that group to 0. P100 (lines 57-74) only checks that the supplied ID equals ASSIGN USERID and INQONLN fills SEC-USER-ID from the same ASSIGN, so P100 never adds an authentication factor.

##### Impact
- A caller can request authorization for another user's ID; the authorization result may not reflect AUTHFILE content at all.
- Authorization data (AUTHFILE) is unmanaged in-repo: no DDL, no grants, no maintenance path.
- Not verified: compile behaviour of the SQLCA host-variable usage and whether RACF resource checks exist at runtime.
findings.recommendation: In P200, obtain the user via EXEC CICS ASSIGN USERID (ignore the COMMAREA value) and use EXEC CICS QUERY SECURITY RESTYPE/RESID or a RACF profile for the resource; if AUTHFILE is kept, select COUNT(*) into a dedicated PIC S9(9) COMP host variable, treat any SQL error as deny, and add AUTHFILE DDL and grants to the repo.
findings.note: Consolidated SECMGR P200 authorization defects (AC-3/AC-6/SC-24): authorizes caller-supplied SEC-USER-ID instead of ASSIGN USERID; COUNT(*) selected INTO the SQLCA group WS-DB2-AREA and compared as a group (fail-open); EVALUATE on request type has no WHEN OTHER so unknown types leave the caller's response code (fail-open). Single fix in SECMGR.cbl: authorize the ASSIGN USERID, select COUNT into a numeric host variable, default-deny on WHEN OTHER/any SQLCODE<>0. Merged duplicates: sfind-7d7afa4bffee4818ae0ead8967ed264d, sfind-901c09358c29478aafa7d2cf1210dafb, sfind-27a12148783f423e91a65aa6ed68e21f. Related (separate fix sites): INQONLN ordering sfind-bef018b2d0b6403bbb8d2437a7c697ec, INQPORT ownership sfind-b7d4a1d950ce437e835788ef10c7b8fb, INQHIST sfind-026ac01e665e41428c0c12812efb51b1.

snippets.commentary: Authorization keyed on caller-supplied SEC-USER-ID with COUNT selected into WS-DB2-AREA.
snippets.code:
P200-CHECK-AUTH.
             EXEC SQL
                  SELECT COUNT(*)
                  INTO :WS-DB2-AREA
                  FROM AUTHFILE
                  WHERE USER_ID = :SEC-USER-ID
                    AND RESOURCE = :SEC-RESOURCE-NAME
                    AND ACCESS_TYPE = :SEC-ACCESS-TYPE
             END-EXEC.
             
             EVALUATE SQLCODE
                 WHEN 0
                      IF WS-DB2-AREA > 0
                         MOVE 0 TO SEC-RESPONSE-CODE
                      ELSE
                         MOVE 'Access denied' 
                           TO SEC-ERROR-INFO
                         MOVE 8 TO SEC-RESPONSE-CODE
                      END-IF
                 WHEN OTHER
                      MOVE 'Authorization check failed' 
                        TO SEC-ERROR-INFO
                      MOVE 12 TO SEC-RESPONSE-CODE
             END-EVALUATE.

snippets.commentary: WS-DB2-AREA is the SQLCA include, not a counter field.
snippets.code:
01  WS-DB2-AREA.
             EXEC SQL INCLUDE SQLCA END-EXEC.

snippets.commentary: Validation only compares the supplied ID to ASSIGN USERID; no ESM call.
snippets.code:
P100-VALIDATE-USER.
             EXEC CICS ASSIGN
                       USERID(WS-USER-ID)
                       RESP(SEC-RESPONSE-CODE)
             END-EXEC.
             
             IF SEC-RESPONSE-CODE = DFHRESP(NORMAL)
                IF SEC-USER-ID = WS-USER-ID
                   MOVE 0 TO SEC-RESPONSE-CODE
                ELSE
                   MOVE 'User validation failed' 
                     TO SEC-ERROR-INFO
                   MOVE 8 TO SEC-RESPONSE-CODE
                END-IF
             ELSE
                MOVE 'Unable to obtain user credentials' 
                  TO SEC-ERROR-INFO
                MOVE 12 TO SEC-RESPONSE-CODE
             END-IF.

findings.title: UTLMNT00 continues processing after file open failures
findings.description:
##### Overview
UTLMNT00's error handler only stops the job after more than 100 errors; failures to open the control, archive or report file are counted and processing proceeds to READ and to archive/cleanup/reorg functions. The function paragraphs (2210-2520) are not present in the file, so the downstream effect could not be traced.

##### Applicability
SC-24 (fail to a known state): this utility performs destructive maintenance (CLEANUP delete-old, REORG delete/define).

##### Evidence
Lines 97-117 PERFORM 9999-ERROR-HANDLER on open failures; lines 176-181 GOBACK only when WS-ERROR-COUNT > 100; lines 122-130 then read CONTROL-FILE and dispatch functions.

##### Impact
- A maintenance run can proceed to delete/redefine steps with no archive or report file open, so archived copies or the run report may be missing.
- Not verified: the missing paragraph implementations.
findings.recommendation: Treat any open failure as fatal: set RETURN-CODE 12, close what is open and GOBACK before 2000-PROCESS.

findings.title: INQONLN dispatches inquiry LINKs before running the SECMGR authorization check
findings.description:
##### Overview
INQONLN's main loop runs the requested inquiry (INQPORT / INQHIST LINK, which sends portfolio data to the terminal) and only afterwards runs P050-SECURITY-CHECK, so the authorization decision cannot stop the data access it is meant to guard. Whether CICS transaction-level security (RACF TCICSTRN for PINQ) is active at runtime is outside the repo and was not verified.

##### Applicability
AC-3 requires approved authorizations to be enforced for logical access; SECMGR is the repo's application-level access enforcement for the PINQ transaction, so the order in which INQONLN calls it decides whether it enforces anything. CICS/RACF transaction security is a separate layer whose evidence must come from the ESM configuration.

##### Evidence
Lines 62-77 evaluate WS-COMMAREA-FUNCTION and PERFORM P300/P400, which LINK INQPORT/INQHIST (lines 101-117). The security check at lines 79-80 and the denial at 82-88 come after that EVALUATE. INQHIST sends HISMAP with history rows itself, so by the time SEC-RESPONSE-CODE is non-zero the data has already been shown.

```
RECEIVE MAP --> EVALUATE --> LINK INQHIST --> SEND MAP(history) --> P050 SECMGR check --> RETURN if denied
```

##### Impact
- Portfolio and transaction-history data reaches users that SECMGR/AUTHFILE would deny.
- Assumes INQPORT behaves like INQHIST (sends its own map); INQPORT was not in this batch.
- Not verified: whether RACF transaction/resource security restricts PINQ at runtime.
findings.recommendation: Move PERFORM P050-SECURITY-CHECK (and the non-zero SEC-RESPONSE-CODE exit) to immediately after RECEIVE MAP and before the EVALUATE, and pass a per-function resource name (e.g. INQPORT/INQHIST) to SECMGR so each inquiry is authorized before it is dispatched.
findings.note: Merged duplicates: sfind-d577c42c52b546d0bdc74ad2814b79a2, sfind-7290cec8edbd46bb958838ab73cf5b66. Related to SECMGR authorization group sfind-ebd8f670cd7b47be83adb0c215e5a38f.

snippets.commentary: Function dispatch to INQPORT/INQHIST runs before P050-SECURITY-CHECK and the denial branch.
snippets.code:
EVALUATE WS-COMMAREA-FUNCTION
                 WHEN 'MENU'
                      PERFORM P200-DISPLAY-MENU
                         THRU P200-EXIT
                 WHEN 'INQP'
                      PERFORM P300-PORTFOLIO-INQUIRY
                         THRU P300-EXIT
                 WHEN 'INQH'
                      PERFORM P400-HISTORY-INQUIRY
                         THRU P400-EXIT
                 WHEN 'EXIT'
                      SET SESSION-TERMINATED TO TRUE
                 WHEN OTHER
                      PERFORM P900-ERROR-ROUTINE
                         THRU P900-EXIT
             END-EVALUATE.
             
             PERFORM P050-SECURITY-CHECK
                THRU P050-EXIT.
                
             IF SEC-RESPONSE-CODE NOT = 0
                MOVE SEC-ERROR-INFO 
                  TO WS-ERROR-MESSAGE
                PERFORM P900-ERROR-ROUTINE
                   THRU P900-EXIT
                EXEC CICS RETURN END-EXEC
             END-IF.

snippets.commentary: P400 LINKs INQHIST, which retrieves and displays history before any authorization.
snippets.code:
P400-HISTORY-INQUIRY.
             EXEC CICS LINK PROGRAM('INQHIST')
                       COMMAREA(WS-COMMAREA)
                       LENGTH(LENGTH OF WS-COMMAREA)
                       RESP(WS-RESPONSE-CODE)
             END-EXEC.
         P400-EXIT.
             EXIT.

snippets.commentary: INQHIST sends the history map to the terminal itself.
snippets.code:
P300-FORMAT-DISPLAY.
             EXEC CICS SEND MAP('HISMAP')
                       MAPSET('INQSET')
                       FROM(WS-HISTORY-TABLE)
                       LENGTH(LENGTH OF WS-HISTORY-TABLE)
                       ERASE
                       RESP(WS-RESPONSE-CODE)
             END-EXEC.

findings.title: ERRHNDL user-facing error message format and timestamp source
findings.description:
##### Artifact
P300 (lines 92-100) builds the message returned to callers as 'Error in <program> - <message> (<trace id>)'. P100 (lines 55-59) timestamps each error with FUNCTION CURRENT-DATE, which carries the local GMT offset, and assigns a FUNCTION RANDOM trace ID when none is supplied.

##### Bears on
SI-11 (content of error messages shown to users) and AU-8 (time-stamp source and UTC offset).

##### Limits
ERR-MESSAGE content is set by callers; this does not show what each caller places in it. The 26-byte ERR-TIMESTAMP holds the 21-character CURRENT-DATE value without conversion to UTC.

snippets.commentary: Timestamp/trace ID assignment and formatted user message.
snippets.code:
P100-INIT-ERROR-HANDLER.
     MOVE DFHCOMMAREA TO WS-ERROR-AREA.
  
     MOVE FUNCTION CURRENT-DATE TO ERR-TIMESTAMP.
  
     IF ERR-TRACE-ID = SPACES
        MOVE FUNCTION RANDOM TO ERR-TRACE-ID
     END-IF.
  P100-EXIT.
     EXIT.
  
  P200-LOG-ERROR.
     MOVE ERR-TIMESTAMP    TO LOG-TIMESTAMP.
     MOVE ERR-PROGRAM      TO LOG-PROGRAM.
     MOVE ERR-PARAGRAPH    TO LOG-PARAGRAPH.
     MOVE ERR-SQLCODE      TO LOG-SQLCODE.
     MOVE ERR-CICS-RESP    TO LOG-CICS-RESP.
     MOVE ERR-SEVERITY     TO LOG-SEVERITY.
     MOVE ERR-MESSAGE      TO LOG-MESSAGE.
     MOVE ERR-TRACE-ID     TO LOG-TRACE-ID.
  
     EXEC SQL
          INSERT INTO ERRLOG
          VALUES (:LOG-TIMESTAMP,
                 :LOG-PROGRAM,
                 :LOG-PARAGRAPH,
                 :LOG-SQLCODE,
                 :LOG-CICS-RESP,
                 :LOG-SEVERITY,
                 :LOG-MESSAGE,
                 :LOG-TRACE-ID)
     END-EXEC.
  
     IF SQLCODE NOT = 0
        MOVE 'Error logging failed' TO ERR-MESSAGE
        SET ERR-FATAL TO TRUE
     END-IF.
  P200-EXIT.
     EXIT.
  
  P300-FORMAT-MESSAGE.
     STRING 'Error in ' DELIMITED BY SIZE
            ERR-PROGRAM DELIMITED BY SPACE
            ' - ' DELIMITED BY SIZE
            ERR-MESSAGE DELIMITED BY SIZE
            ' (' DELIMITED BY SIZE
            ERR-TRACE-ID DELIMITED BY SIZE
            ')' DELIMITED BY SIZE
            INTO ERR-MESSAGE.
  P300-EXIT.
     EXIT.

findings.title: DB2 template models data mutations with no audit record
findings.description:
##### Overview
The DB2HNDL template, which models how programs should access DB2, performs INSERT, UPDATE and DELETE on PORTFOLIO with no call to the repo's audit routine (AUDPROC) or any audit insert. It is a template, so exposure is limited to code copied from it.

##### Applicability
AU-12 / AU-2: data modifications to portfolio master records are audit events; templates set the pattern developers follow (SA-15).

##### Evidence
Lines 106-117 (INSERT), 187-195 (UPDATE), 201-207 (DELETE) are followed only by 9000-CHECK-SQL-STATUS; no audit call appears anywhere in the file.

##### Impact
- Programs derived from the template would mutate portfolio data with no before/after audit record.
- Not verified which production programs were derived from it.
findings.recommendation: Add an audit step to the template (CALL AUDPROC with user, action, key and before/after images) after each successful mutation within the same unit of work.
findings.note: src/templates/ is developer template code, not deployed system code; no requirement is violated by the deployed system.

findings.title: ERRHNDL ERRLOG insert mismatches table schema and omits user identity
findings.description:
##### Overview
ERRHNDL inserts eight positional values into ERRLOG, but the committed ERRLOG DDL defines ten NOT NULL-heavy columns with different types and order, so the insert cannot succeed against that table; the record also carries no user ID or terminal.

##### Applicability
AU-12 (generate the audit records defined) and AU-3 (identity and outcome in records): ERRHNDL is the central online error/event logger. AU-5 covers what happens when logging fails.

##### Evidence
ERRHNDL lines 73-83 `INSERT INTO ERRLOG VALUES` with timestamp, program, paragraph (X30), SQLCODE, CICS RESP, severity (X1), message, trace ID. ERRLOG.sql lines 15-25 expects ERROR_TIMESTAMP, PROGRAM_ID, ERROR_TYPE CHAR(1), ERROR_SEVERITY INTEGER, ERROR_CODE CHAR(8), ERROR_MESSAGE, PROCESS_DATE, PROCESS_TIME, USER_ID NOT NULL, ADDITIONAL_INFO. Line 55 also feeds CURRENT-DATE text into the TIMESTAMP column. On failure lines 85-88 set ERR-FATAL, which P400 turns into ERR-ABEND, so callers such as INQONLN abend.

```
online error --> ERRHNDL INSERT (8 cols) --> ERRLOG (10 cols) --> SQL error --> ERR-FATAL --> ABEND, no record
```

##### Impact
- Online errors (including security-check failures routed here) are never recorded in ERRLOG and every logged warning becomes an abend.
- Even if aligned, records would lack the user identity AU-3 requires.
- Assumes the deployed ERRLOG matches src/database/db2/ERRLOG.sql.
findings.recommendation: Use an explicit column list matching ERRLOG.sql, map severity to the INTEGER scale, populate PROCESS_DATE/TIME and USER_ID (from EXEC CICS ASSIGN USERID) and use CURRENT TIMESTAMP; on insert failure write a fallback record (e.g. CSMT/TD queue) before deciding to abend.

P200-LOG-ERROR.
     MOVE ERR-TIMESTAMP    TO LOG-TIMESTAMP.
     MOVE ERR-PROGRAM      TO LOG-PROGRAM.
     MOVE ERR-PARAGRAPH    TO LOG-PARAGRAPH.
     MOVE ERR-SQLCODE      TO LOG-SQLCODE.
     MOVE ERR-CICS-RESP    TO LOG-CICS-RESP.
     MOVE ERR-SEVERITY     TO LOG-SEVERITY.
     MOVE ERR-MESSAGE      TO LOG-MESSAGE.
     MOVE ERR-TRACE-ID     TO LOG-TRACE-ID.
  
     EXEC SQL
          INSERT INTO ERRLOG
          VALUES (:LOG-TIMESTAMP,
                 :LOG-PROGRAM,
                 :LOG-PARAGRAPH,
                 :LOG-SQLCODE,
                 :LOG-CICS-RESP,
                 :LOG-SEVERITY,
                 :LOG-MESSAGE,
                 :LOG-TRACE-ID)
     END-EXEC.
  
     IF SQLCODE NOT = 0
        MOVE 'Error logging failed' TO ERR-MESSAGE
        SET ERR-FATAL TO TRUE
     END-IF.
  P200-EXIT.
     EXIT.

findings.title: DB2RECV bounded reconnect retry and rollback paths
findings.description:
##### Artifact
P100 (lines 62-81) retries DB2ONLN connect up to WS-MAX-RETRIES = 3 times with EXEC CICS DELAY INTERVAL(2) between attempts and sets RECV-FAILED with response -1 after exhaustion. P200 (lines 111-122) issues EXEC SQL ROLLBACK and reports failure via RECV-FAILED. P300 (lines 125-143) routes cursor failures to ERRHNDL. Only P300 writes an error log entry; P100 and P200 outcomes are returned to the caller without being logged.

##### Bears on
SC-24 (fail in known state) and AU-2 (event types logged for recovery events).

##### Limits
Does not show how callers act on RECV-FAILED (INQHIST continues processing; see INQHIST finding), nor whether SQL ROLLBACK is honoured inside the CICS unit of work versus EXEC CICS SYNCPOINT ROLLBACK at runtime.

snippets.commentary: Bounded retry loop, delay, and rollback handling.
snippets.code:
P100-RECOVER-CONNECTION.
             MOVE 0 TO WS-RETRY-COUNT.
             
             PERFORM UNTIL WS-RETRY-COUNT >= WS-MAX-RETRIES
                PERFORM P110-ATTEMPT-RECONNECT
                   THRU P110-EXIT
                   
                IF RECV-SUCCESS
                   EXIT PERFORM
                ELSE
                   PERFORM P120-WAIT-INTERVAL
                      THRU P120-EXIT
                   ADD 1 TO WS-RETRY-COUNT
                END-IF
             END-PERFORM.
             
             IF WS-RETRY-COUNT >= WS-MAX-RETRIES
                SET RECV-FAILED TO TRUE
                MOVE -1 TO RECV-RESPONSE-CODE
             END-IF.
         P100-EXIT.
             EXIT.
             
         P110-ATTEMPT-RECONNECT.
             MOVE 'C' TO DB2-REQUEST-TYPE OF WS-DB2-REQUEST.
             
             EXEC CICS LINK PROGRAM('DB2ONLN')
                       COMMAREA(WS-DB2-REQUEST)
                       LENGTH(LENGTH OF WS-DB2-REQUEST)
             END-EXEC.
             
             IF DB2-RESPONSE-CODE OF WS-DB2-REQUEST = 0
                SET RECV-SUCCESS TO TRUE
                MOVE 0 TO RECV-RESPONSE-CODE
             ELSE
                SET RECV-RETRY TO TRUE
                MOVE DB2-SQLCODE OF WS-DB2-REQUEST 
                  TO RECV-SQLCODE
             END-IF.
         P110-EXIT.
             EXIT.
             
         P120-WAIT-INTERVAL.
             EXEC CICS DELAY
                       INTERVAL(WS-RETRY-INTERVAL)
             END-EXEC.
         P120-EXIT.
             EXIT.
             
         P200-RECOVER-TRANSACTION.
             EXEC SQL ROLLBACK END-EXEC.
             
             IF SQLCODE = 0
                SET RECV-SUCCESS TO TRUE
                MOVE 0 TO RECV-RESPONSE-CODE
             ELSE
                SET RECV-FAILED TO TRUE
                MOVE SQLCODE TO RECV-SQLCODE
                MOVE -1 TO RECV-RESPONSE-CODE
             END-IF.
         P200-EXIT.

findings.title: Conversational RECEIVE MAP loop has no inactivity timeout
findings.description:
##### Overview
INQONLN holds the task in a conversational loop that waits on RECEIVE MAP until the user enters EXIT; the program sets no inactivity limit, so termination after idle time depends entirely on CICS terminal/transaction configuration outside this program.

##### Applicability
AC-12 and SC-10 require sessions/connections to be terminated after defined conditions such as inactivity. The program owns the session loop; the CSD for PINQ (src/cics/PORTDFN.csd) defines no RTIMOUT, so evidence of an idle timeout must come from runtime CICS SIT/terminal/RACF settings.

##### Evidence
Lines 46-48 loop P100 UNTIL SESSION-TERMINATED; line 56 RECEIVE MAP is issued with no timeout handling, and only the 'EXIT' function (line 72-73) ends the loop.

##### Impact
- An unattended terminal keeps an authenticated inquiry session open indefinitely unless runtime config intervenes.
- Not verified: RTIMOUT/SIT ICVR/terminal timeout settings in the deployed CICS region.
findings.recommendation: Convert to pseudo-conversational RETURN TRANSID with COMMAREA, or define RTIMOUT on the PINQ transaction and handle the AKCT/timeout path to end the session.

snippets.commentary: Loop waits on RECEIVE MAP until the user exits; no idle-time limit.
snippets.code:
PERFORM P100-PROCESS-REQUEST
                THRU P100-EXIT
                UNTIL SESSION-TERMINATED.
                
             EXEC CICS RETURN 
             END-EXEC.
             
         P100-PROCESS-REQUEST.
             MOVE LOW-VALUES TO WS-COMMAREA.
             
             EXEC CICS RECEIVE MAP('INQMAP')
                       MAPSET('INQSET')
                       INTO(WS-COMMAREA)
                       RESP(WS-RESPONSE-CODE)
             END-EXEC.

findings.title: AUDITLOG record omits outcome and object; timestamp format unsuitable
findings.description:
##### Overview
The only security audit record written online (P300) stores timestamp, user, terminal, transaction, resource and access type, but no event outcome and no accessed object (account). The timestamp is FUNCTION CURRENT-DATE moved into a 26-byte field and inserted into a column named TIMESTAMP; AUDITLOG has no DDL in the repo, so the column type and whether the insert succeeds could not be confirmed.

##### Applicability
AU-3 requires records to establish the type, outcome and subjects/objects of an event; AU-8 requires time stamps with UTC mapping. P300 is the audit-record generator for online access.

##### Evidence
Lines 117-125 insert six columns, none carrying outcome or account number. Line 106 uses CURRENT-DATE (YYYYMMDDhhmmsshh±hhmm, 21 chars) rather than a DB2 TIMESTAMP/CURRENT TIMESTAMP value. INQONLN only calls P300 after success, so no outcome field exists to distinguish events.

##### Impact
- Audit trail cannot show which account was viewed or whether access was granted.
- If AUDITLOG.TIMESTAMP is a DB2 TIMESTAMP, the CURRENT-DATE string will be rejected and every audit insert fails (response 12). Needs validation against the real table definition.
findings.recommendation: Add OUTCOME and OBJECT_ID (account number) columns to AUDITLOG and pass them from the caller; use CURRENT TIMESTAMP (or a UTC-normalized value with the offset stored) in the INSERT; commit the AUDITLOG DDL to the repo.

snippets.commentary: Audit row fields and CURRENT-DATE timestamp source.
snippets.code:
P300-LOG-ACCESS.
             MOVE FUNCTION CURRENT-DATE TO WS-TIMESTAMP.
             
             EXEC CICS ASSIGN
                       USERID(WS-USER-ID)
                       TERMID(WS-TERMINAL-ID)
                       TRANSID(WS-TRANSACTION-ID)
             END-EXEC.
             
             MOVE SEC-RESOURCE-NAME TO WS-PROGRAM-NAME.
             MOVE SEC-ACCESS-TYPE TO WS-ACCESS-TYPE.
             
             EXEC SQL
                  INSERT INTO AUDITLOG
                  (TIMESTAMP, USER_ID, TERMINAL_ID, 
                   TRANS_ID, PROGRAM, ACCESS_TYPE)
                  VALUES
                  (:WS-TIMESTAMP, :WS-USER-ID, :WS-TERMINAL-ID,
                   :WS-TRANSACTION-ID, :WS-PROGRAM-NAME, 
                   :WS-ACCESS-TYPE)
             END-EXEC.
             
             IF SQLCODE = 0
                MOVE 0 TO SEC-RESPONSE-CODE
             ELSE
                MOVE 'Audit logging failed' 
                  TO SEC-ERROR-INFO
                MOVE 12 TO SEC-RESPONSE-CODE
             END-IF.

findings.title: SECMGR P100 relies on CICS ASSIGN USERID for user identity
findings.description:
##### Artifact
SECMGR P100 (lines 56-74) issues EXEC CICS ASSIGN USERID and compares the result to the caller-supplied SEC-USER-ID; it contains no password handling, no failed-attempt counter, and no lockout. Authentication of the terminal user is performed by CICS sign-on before the program runs.

##### Bears on
IA-2, AC-7, IA-5: user authentication, unsuccessful-logon limits and authenticator management are handed to CICS sign-on and the external security manager (RACF/ACF2/TSS). Evidence for logon-attempt limits, lockout and password/MFA policy must come from the ESM and CICS SIT (SEC=YES) configuration.

##### Limits
Does not show whether CICS security is enabled, which ESM is used, or any ESM parameter values.

snippets.commentary: User identity obtained from CICS ASSIGN USERID.
snippets.code:
P100-VALIDATE-USER.
             EXEC CICS ASSIGN
                       USERID(WS-USER-ID)
                       RESP(SEC-RESPONSE-CODE)
             END-EXEC.
             
             IF SEC-RESPONSE-CODE = DFHRESP(NORMAL)
                IF SEC-USER-ID = WS-USER-ID
                   MOVE 0 TO SEC-RESPONSE-CODE
                ELSE
                   MOVE 'User validation failed' 
                     TO SEC-ERROR-INFO
                   MOVE 8 TO SEC-RESPONSE-CODE
                END-IF
             ELSE
                MOVE 'Unable to obtain user credentials' 
                  TO SEC-ERROR-INFO
                MOVE 12 TO SEC-RESPONSE-CODE
             END-IF.

findings.title: INQHIST continues to query and display after DB2 connect failure
findings.description:
##### Overview
When DB2ONLN and DB2RECV both fail, INQHIST's error routine only copies SQLCODE into the COMMAREA and returns to the caller paragraph; the main line then still runs the history query and SEND MAP.

##### Applicability
SC-24 requires failing to a known state on defined failures; the DB2 connection failure path is explicitly handled in this program.

##### Evidence
Lines 103-121: on RECV-FAILED it PERFORMs P999 (lines 187-191), which does not RETURN or set a stop flag; lines 72-76 then unconditionally PERFORM P200-GET-HISTORY and P300-FORMAT-DISPLAY. On RECV-SUCCESS, line 113 recursively PERFORMs P150 from inside itself, which has undefined COBOL behaviour. Line 170 moves CURS-DATA-AREA into the display table whenever CURS-RESPONSE-CODE >= 0.

##### Impact
- The user is shown an unpopulated or partial history screen instead of a defined error state; the error message set at line 116-117 is never sent.
- Not verified: runtime behaviour of the recursive PERFORM.
findings.recommendation: Make P999 send an error map (or set INQCOM-RESPONSE-CODE) and EXEC CICS RETURN; gate P200/P300 on a successful connection flag; replace the recursive PERFORM with a bounded loop.

snippets.commentary: Connect failure path and recursive retry.
snippets.code:
P150-DB2-CONNECT.
             MOVE 'C' TO DB2-REQUEST-TYPE.
             
             EXEC CICS LINK PROGRAM('DB2ONLN')
                       COMMAREA(WS-DB2-REQUEST)
                       LENGTH(LENGTH OF WS-DB2-REQUEST)
             END-EXEC.
             
             IF DB2-RESPONSE-CODE NOT = 0
                MOVE 'C' TO RECV-REQUEST-TYPE
                MOVE 'INQHIST' TO RECV-PROGRAM
                MOVE DB2-SQLCODE TO RECV-SQLCODE
                
                EXEC CICS LINK PROGRAM('DB2RECV')
                          COMMAREA(WS-RECOVERY-REQUEST)
                          LENGTH(LENGTH OF WS-RECOVERY-REQUEST)
                END-EXEC
                
                IF RECV-SUCCESS
                   PERFORM P150-DB2-CONNECT
                      THRU P150-EXIT
                ELSE
                   MOVE RECV-MESSAGE 
                     TO INQCOM-ERROR-MSG OF WS-COMMAREA
                   PERFORM P999-ERROR-ROUTINE
                      THRU P999-EXIT
                END-IF
             END-IF.
             
             MOVE DB2-CONNECTION-TOKEN 
               TO WS-DB2-TOKEN.
         P150-EXIT.

snippets.commentary: Main line runs query and display regardless of connect outcome.
snippets.code:
PROCEDURE DIVISION.
             PERFORM P100-INIT-PROGRAM
                THRU P100-EXIT.
                
             PERFORM P200-GET-HISTORY
                THRU P200-EXIT.
                
             PERFORM P300-FORMAT-DISPLAY
                THRU P300-EXIT.
                
             EXEC CICS RETURN END-EXEC.

snippets.commentary: Error routine neither returns nor flags processing to stop.
snippets.code:
P999-ERROR-ROUTINE.
             MOVE SQLCODE 
               TO INQCOM-RESPONSE-CODE OF WS-COMMAREA.
             MOVE WS-COMMAREA TO DFHCOMMAREA.
         P999-EXIT.

findings.title: Failed validations and access denials leave no audit record
findings.description:
##### Overview
INQONLN asks SECMGR to write an AUDITLOG row (request type 'L') only when both validation and authorization succeed; denied or failed security decisions are not recorded anywhere except, at most, the ERRHNDL error path.

##### Applicability
AU-2/AU-12 require the system to generate audit records for security-relevant event types; unsuccessful access attempts are a core event type. SECMGR P300 is the repo's security audit writer, so the decision of when to call it lives here.

##### Evidence
Lines 151-167: the 'L' audit call is nested inside both `IF SEC-RESPONSE-CODE = 0` branches. Lines 82-88 handle a non-zero code by calling P900 (ERRHNDL with ERR-WARNING) and RETURN, with no SECMGR audit. ERRHNDL's ERRLOG row carries no user ID (see ERRHNDL finding).

##### Impact
- No record of who was denied, from which terminal, for which resource.
- Repeated denied attempts cannot be detected (bears on AC-2(12) monitoring).
- Not verified: whether RACF SMF records capture CICS-level denials at runtime.
findings.recommendation: Call SECMGR with request type 'L' on every outcome of validation and authorization, passing the outcome (success/denied/error) so P300 records it; extend AUDITLOG with an outcome column.

snippets.commentary: Audit ('L') request is issued only on the success path of both checks.
snippets.code:
P050-SECURITY-CHECK.
             MOVE 'V' TO SEC-REQUEST-TYPE.
             
             EXEC CICS ASSIGN
                       USERID(SEC-USER-ID)
             END-EXEC.
             
             EXEC CICS LINK PROGRAM('SECMGR')
                       COMMAREA(WS-SECURITY-REQUEST)
                       LENGTH(LENGTH OF WS-SECURITY-REQUEST)
             END-EXEC.
             
             IF SEC-RESPONSE-CODE = 0
                MOVE 'A' TO SEC-REQUEST-TYPE
                MOVE 'INQONLN' TO SEC-RESOURCE-NAME
                MOVE 'READ' TO SEC-ACCESS-TYPE
                
                EXEC CICS LINK PROGRAM('SECMGR')
                          COMMAREA(WS-SECURITY-REQUEST)
                          LENGTH(LENGTH OF WS-SECURITY-REQUEST)
                END-EXEC
                
                IF SEC-RESPONSE-CODE = 0
                   MOVE 'L' TO SEC-REQUEST-TYPE
                   
                   EXEC CICS LINK PROGRAM('SECMGR')
                             COMMAREA(WS-SECURITY-REQUEST)
                             LENGTH(LENGTH OF WS-SECURITY-REQUEST)
                   END-EXEC
                END-IF
             END-IF.

snippets.commentary: Denial path goes to the error routine and RETURN without any audit call.
snippets.code:
IF SEC-RESPONSE-CODE NOT = 0
                MOVE SEC-ERROR-INFO 
                  TO WS-ERROR-MESSAGE
                PERFORM P900-ERROR-ROUTINE
                   THRU P900-EXIT
                EXEC CICS RETURN END-EXEC
             END-IF.

findings.title: CURSMGR executes caller-supplied SQL text with no authorization or validation
findings.description:
##### Overview
CURSMGR accepts a 240-byte SQL statement and cursor name from its COMMAREA and declares/opens a cursor over it, with no check of who the caller is, which tables the statement touches, or what the statement contains. The program as committed is incomplete (P300/P400 paragraphs are absent and DECLARE with host-variable names is not valid static SQL), so the effect depends on how it is completed; the design intent is a generic SQL executor.

##### Applicability
AC-6 / AC-3 (only authorized accesses through processes acting for users) and SI-10 (validate inputs): CURSMGR runs under the PINQ plan's DB2 authority (DB2ENTRY PORTDB2, PLAN PORTPLAN), so the statement text is the access decision.

##### Evidence
Lines 34-35 define CURS-NAME and CURS-STMT in the linkage area; lines 70-72 declare a cursor directly from them and line 84 opens it. No SECMGR call, no allow-list, no statement check exists anywhere in the program.

##### Impact
- Any program that can LINK CURSMGR can read any table PORTPLAN can read, bypassing SECMGR.
- Not verified: final implementation of FETCH/CLOSE and the PORTPLAN package grants.
findings.recommendation: Replace the free-form statement with a fixed set of static cursors selected by a request code (e.g. HISTORY_CURSOR with a bound ACCOUNT_NO host variable), and reject unknown codes; if dynamic SQL is retained, PREPARE only from an allow-listed statement table and authorize the caller via SECMGR first.

snippets.commentary: Statement text and cursor name come from the caller's COMMAREA.
snippets.code:
LINKAGE SECTION.
         01  CURSOR-REQUEST-AREA.
             05 CURS-REQUEST-TYPE     PIC X.
                88 CURS-DECLARE           VALUE 'D'.
                88 CURS-OPEN              VALUE 'O'.
                88 CURS-FETCH             VALUE 'F'.
                88 CURS-CLOSE             VALUE 'C'.
             05 CURS-NAME             PIC X(18).
             05 CURS-STMT             PIC X(240).
             05 CURS-ARRAY-FETCH      PIC X VALUE 'N'.
                88 USE-ARRAY-FETCH         VALUE 'Y'.
                88 NO-ARRAY-FETCH          VALUE 'N'.
             05 CURS-RESPONSE-CODE    PIC S9(8) COMP.
             05 CURS-DATA-AREA        PIC X(3000).
             05 CURS-DATA-LENGTH      PIC S9(4) COMP.

snippets.commentary: Cursor declared and opened directly from caller text with no check.
snippets.code:
P100-DECLARE-CURSOR.
             MOVE 0 TO CURS-RESPONSE-CODE.
             
             IF USE-ARRAY-FETCH
                MOVE WS-MAX-ROWS TO WS-ARRAY-SIZE
             ELSE
                MOVE 1 TO WS-ARRAY-SIZE
             END-IF.
             
             EXEC SQL DECLARE :CURS-NAME CURSOR FOR
                  :CURS-STMT
             END-EXEC.
             
             IF SQLCODE NOT = 0
                MOVE SQLCODE TO CURS-RESPONSE-CODE
             END-IF.
         P100-EXIT.
             EXIT.
             
         P200-OPEN-CURSOR.
             MOVE 0 TO WS-FETCH-COUNT.
             MOVE 0 TO WS-ROWS-FETCHED.
             
             EXEC SQL OPEN :CURS-NAME END-EXEC.
             
             IF SQLCODE = 0
                MOVE 0 TO CURS-RESPONSE-CODE
             ELSE
                MOVE SQLCODE TO CURS-RESPONSE-CODE
             END-IF.

findings.title: DB2ONLN connection limit counter resets on every LINK
findings.description:
##### Overview
The 100-connection cap is enforced against WS-ACTIVE-CONNECTIONS held in WORKING-STORAGE; CICS gives each LINK a fresh copy of WORKING-STORAGE, so the counter starts at 0 every call and the cap never triggers.

##### Applicability
SC-5 (limit effects of denial-of-service) and AC-10 (limit concurrent sessions): DB2ONLN is the repo's only connection-limiting control for online DB2 access.

##### Evidence
Lines 20-22 initialise the counters with VALUE clauses in WORKING-STORAGE; line 55 compares against WS-MAX-CONNECTIONS; lines 70 and 95 increment/decrement a counter that is discarded at RETURN (line 52). Nothing persists it in a TS queue, CWA, or shared storage.

##### Impact
- The intended limit on concurrent DB2 connections is not enforced; protection rests on CICS DB2ENTRY THREADLIMIT/DB2CONN settings outside this program.
- P300 also returns this per-call counter as status, so monitoring based on it is meaningless.
- Not verified: runtime DB2CONN/DB2ENTRY thread limits.
findings.recommendation: Rely on and document CICS DB2ENTRY/DB2CONN THREADLIMIT for PORTDB2, or keep the counter in shared storage (CWA or a recoverable TS queue with ENQ) so the cap applies across tasks.

snippets.commentary: Counters live in per-task WORKING-STORAGE.
snippets.code:
01  WS-POOL-STATS.
             05 WS-TOTAL-CONNECTIONS    PIC S9(8) COMP VALUE 0.
             05 WS-ACTIVE-CONNECTIONS   PIC S9(8) COMP VALUE 0.
             05 WS-AVAILABLE-CONNECTIONS PIC S9(8) COMP VALUE 0.
             05 WS-MAX-CONNECTIONS      PIC S9(8) COMP VALUE 100.

snippets.commentary: Limit check against a counter that is always zero on entry.
snippets.code:
P100-PROCESS-CONNECT.
             IF WS-ACTIVE-CONNECTIONS < WS-MAX-CONNECTIONS
                PERFORM P110-ESTABLISH-CONNECTION
                   THRU P110-EXIT
             ELSE
                MOVE 'Maximum connections reached' 
                  TO DB2-ERROR-MSG
                MOVE -1 TO DB2-RESPONSE-CODE
             END-IF.
         P100-EXIT.

findings.title: INQHIST returns account history with no account-level authorization
findings.description:
##### Overview
INQHIST retrieves and displays POSHIST transaction history for the account number entered on the screen without checking that the signed-on user is entitled to that account; SECMGR is only asked (by INQONLN, after the fact) about the generic resource 'INQONLN' READ.

##### Applicability
AC-3 requires enforcement of approved authorizations for access to information; per-account client history is the protected object here.

##### Evidence
INQHIST lines 129-135 build `SELECT ... FROM POSHIST WHERE ACCOUNT_NO = ?` for the COMMAREA account (INQCOM-ACCOUNT-NO, populated from RECEIVE MAP in INQONLN line 56) and lines 177-184 send the rows. No SECMGR call or ownership check exists in the program; INQONLN lines 152-153 authorize only resource 'INQONLN'.

##### Impact
- Any user permitted to run PINQ can view the transaction history of any account number they type.
- Not verified: whether RACF/DB2 row-level controls exist at runtime.
findings.recommendation: Before querying, call SECMGR with request 'A', the ASSIGN user ID, and the account number (or an account-group resource) as SEC-RESOURCE-NAME, and stop with a denial message if it fails; record the account in the audit request.

snippets.commentary: History query keyed only by the user-entered account number.
snippets.code:
P200-GET-HISTORY.
             MOVE 'SELECT TRANS_DATE, TRANS_TYPE, TRANS_UNITS, ' &
                  'TRANS_PRICE, TRANS_AMOUNT ' &
                  'FROM POSHIST ' &
                  'WHERE ACCOUNT_NO = ? ' &
                  'ORDER BY TRANS_DATE DESC' 
               TO CURS-STMT.

snippets.commentary: Authorization request names the transaction program, not the account.
snippets.code:
IF SEC-RESPONSE-CODE = 0
                MOVE 'A' TO SEC-REQUEST-TYPE
                MOVE 'INQONLN' TO SEC-RESOURCE-NAME
                MOVE 'READ' TO SEC-ACCESS-TYPE
                
                EXEC CICS LINK PROGRAM('SECMGR')
                          COMMAREA(WS-SECURITY-REQUEST)
                          LENGTH(LENGTH OF WS-SECURITY-REQUEST)
                END-EXEC

findings.title: Batch control constants: status codes, RC thresholds, restart limit
findings.description:
##### Artifact

Defines process statuses (R/A/W/D/E, 9-13), return-code thresholds 0/4/8/12/16 (17-21), BCT-MAX-RESTARTS 3 and wait limits (25-28), and standard messages including 'Process failed - check errors' (57-64).

SC-24 (fail in known state: defined error status and bounded restart count for batch processes).

##### Limits

Constants only; does not show that programs honour the restart limit or roll back on BCT-RC-ERROR or worse.

        *    Return Code Thresholds

findings.title: POSHIST account and transaction history stored with no at-rest encryption
findings.description:
##### Overview

findings.title: AUD-TIMESTAMP has no time-zone/UTC field and writers fill it inconsistently
findings.description:
##### Overview

The audit timestamp is a 26-byte local timestamp with no UTC offset field, and the programs that populate it use two different sources and formats, so audit time cannot be mapped reliably to UTC or correlated across writers.

##### Applicability

AU-8 (audit time stamps that use UTC or have a fixed local-time offset from UTC) for the system's audit record.

##### Evidence

AUDITLOG.cpy line 9 defines AUD-TIMESTAMP PIC X(26) with no offset field. AUDPROC.cbl line 60 fills it via ACCEPT ... FROM TIME STAMP (local, no zone); PORTTRAN.cbl line 252 moves FUNCTION CURRENT-DATE (21-char YYYYMMDDhhmmssccsHHMM incl. offset) into the same 26-byte field, a different layout.

##### Impact

- Audit records from AUDPROC carry no UTC mapping; records from PORTTRAN use a different format in the same field, breaking ordering/reporting in RPTAUD00.
- Assumed the host clock is local time; not verified.
findings.recommendation: Populate AUD-TIMESTAMP from FUNCTION CURRENT-DATE in one shared routine (AUDPROC) and either store UTC or add an AUD-UTC-OFFSET X(5) field; convert to one documented format.
findings.note: AU-8 group: audit/error timestamps produced inconsistently without UTC offset across writers. Single fix: add a UTC/offset field to AUDITLOG.cpy and a shared timestamp routine. findings.title: ERRLOG_CLEANUP deletes error-log rows with unbounded caller retention, unrecorded
findings.description:
##### Overview

The cleanup procedure deletes every ERRLOG row older than a caller-supplied number of days with no minimum, no record of the purge, and no EXECUTE grant defined in the DDL, so whoever can run it can erase the error trail (RETENTION_DAYS 0 deletes all but today's rows).

##### Applicability

SI-12 (manage and retain information per defined requirements) and AU-9 (protect logged information from unauthorized deletion). ERRLOG records program errors with USER_ID and is read by the RPTAUD00 audit report job; organisational retention periods are not defined in the repo.

##### Evidence

ERRLOG.sql 59-65 delete by `CURRENT DATE - RETENTION_DAYS DAYS` with no validation or audit insert; grants at 55-56 cover only SELECT/INSERT on the table, with no GRANT EXECUTE that would restrict who can call the procedure.

##### Impact

- Error/security event history can be removed without trace.
- Retention period is undefined in code; not verified whether an external scheduler passes a fixed value or who holds EXECUTE (DB2 catalog).
findings.recommendation: Enforce a minimum retention (reject RETENTION_DAYS below the organisational value), insert a purge record (user, cutoff, rows deleted) into an audit table in the same unit of work, and GRANT EXECUTE only to a dedicated maintenance authority.

snippets.commentary: procedure deletes by caller-supplied age with no checks or audit.
snippets.code:
CREATE PROCEDURE ERRLOG_CLEANUP
    (IN RETENTION_DAYS INTEGER)
    LANGUAGE SQL
  BEGIN
    DELETE FROM ERRLOG
    WHERE PROCESS_DATE < CURRENT DATE - RETENTION_DAYS DAYS;
  END;

findings.title: SECMGR security program and PINQ transaction defined without isolation or resource security
findings.description:
##### Overview

The CSD runs the security manager SECMGR in user key like every other program and defines PINQ with no RESSEC/CMDSEC, so in this repo nothing isolates the security function or requests per-resource checks; region SIT settings (SEC=, STGPROT=, XFCT etc.) outside the repo could still enforce them.

##### Applicability

SC-3 (security function isolation) and AC-3/AC-6 (access enforcement / least privilege on CICS resources). The CSD is the system's resource-definition artifact; region-level SIT and RACF profiles are outside the repo.

##### Evidence

PORTDFN.csd 56-61 defines SECMGR with EXECKEY(USER), identical to the application programs at 14-54; the PINQ transaction at 6-11 specifies only PROGRAM/PROFILE/STATUS, with no RESSEC(YES) or CMDSEC(YES).

##### Impact

- Security-function storage is not isolated from application programs by the definition; any user-key program can overwrite it if storage protection is off.
- Resource-level security on POSFILE and DB2 access depends entirely on region defaults.
- Not verified: SIT SEC/STGPROT/RESSEC values and RACF TCICSTRN/FCICSFCT profiles.
findings.recommendation: Define SECMGR with EXECKEY(CICS) (or isolate it in its own transaction) and set RESSEC(YES) and CMDSEC(YES) on PINQ, with matching RACF resource profiles.

         PROFILE(DFHCICST)

         GROUP(PORTGRP)
         STATUS(ENABLED)

findings.title: cobol_fields CLI argument parsing and strict-by-default record decoding
findings.description:
##### Artifact

Developer CLI (`layout`, `dump`, `diff`). `--dialect` is restricted to `choices=DIALECTS` (line 78); copybook and record files are read from user-supplied paths (lines 36, 43). `dump` warns on stderr when file length is not a multiple of the record length (44-46) and decodes with `strict=not args.lenient` (49), so invalid sign/zone bytes raise unless `--lenient` is given. `dump` prints every decoded field value to stdout (53-58).

##### Bears on

SI-10 (validity checks on copybook/record inputs to the migration-validation tooling) and SI-11 (what error/diagnostic output reveals).

##### Limits

This is an offline developer tool, not part of the mainframe runtime; it shows no authentication or access control on the files it reads, which is left to the workstation's file permissions. `diff` always runs with `strict=False` (line 65).

snippets.commentary: dump reads a record file, warns on partial records and decodes strictly unless --lenient.
argparse definition; dialect restricted to known choices.
snippets.code:
def main(argv=None) -> int:
      p = argparse.ArgumentParser(prog="cobol_fields", description=__doc__,
                                  formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter)
      common = argparse.ArgumentParser(add_help=False)
      common.add_argument("--dialect", choices=DIALECTS, default="ibm",
                          help="ibm: COMP 2/4/8 bytes, EBCDIC cp037 (default). gnucobol: 1/2/4/8, ASCII. "
                               "gnucobol-ibm: cobc -std=ibm (2/4/8 bytes, ASCII)")
      common.add_argument("--encoding", help="override text encoding, e.g. cp037, cp1047, ascii, latin-1")
      common.add_argument("--record", help="01-level name when the copybook defines several")
      sub = p.add_subparsers(dest="cmd", required=True)
  
      s = sub.add_parser("layout", parents=[common], help="print offsets, lengths and definitions")
      s.add_argument("copybook")
      s.set_defaults(fn=cmd_layout)
  
      s = sub.add_parser("dump", parents=[common], help="decode a record file")
      s.add_argument("copybook")
      s.add_argument("file")
      s.add_argument("--json", action="store_true")
      s.add_argument("--lenient", action="store_true", help="do not fail on invalid sign/zone bytes")
      s.set_defaults(fn=cmd_dump)
  
      s = sub.add_parser("diff", parents=[common], help="compare two record files field by field (exit 1 on mismatch)")
      s.add_argument("copybook")
      s.add_argument("expected", help="reference file, normally written by the COBOL program")
      s.add_argument("actual", help="file written by the migrated code")
      s.add_argument("--ignore", action="append", metavar="FIELD",
                     help="field to skip (e.g. an audit timestamp); repeatable")
      s.add_argument("--max", type=int, default=50, help="max mismatches to print")
      s.set_defaults(fn=cmd_diff)
  
      args = p.parse_args(argv)
      return args.fn(args)

findings.title: Checkpoint record carries no integrity check and CKPRST restart routines are empty
findings.description:
##### Overview

The checkpoint VSAM record stores 400 bytes of opaque restart state with no checksum, hash or verification field, and the CKPRST module that uses this copybook implements init/take/commit/restart as empty paragraphs, so restart cannot resume from a verified state.

##### Applicability

SI-7/SI-7(1) (integrity checks on information at security-relevant transitional states) and SC-24 (fail to a known state preserving state information) for the batch checkpoint/restart framework.

##### Evidence

CKPRST.cpy 52-56 defines CHECKPOINT-RECORD as key plus CKR-DATA X(400) with no integrity field; 6-47 define the control area (last key, counters, restart mode) with nothing verifying them. CKPRST.cbl 43-57 contains only comments in PROC-INIT, PROC-TAKE-CHECKPOINT, PROC-COMMIT-CHECKPOINT and PROC-RESTART.

##### Impact

- Restarted batch runs (BCHCTL00, PRCSEQ00, RCVPRC00, HISTLD00 copy CKPRST) have no verified restart point; a corrupted or altered checkpoint is accepted and can cause duplicate or skipped position/history updates.
- No record of checkpoint commits exists to support recovery.
- Not verified: whether production uses a different checkpoint implementation.
findings.recommendation: Add a CKR-CHECKSUM (e.g. SHA-256 via ICSF over CKR-KEY+CKR-DATA) written at PROC-TAKE/COMMIT and verified in PROC-RESTART, failing the job if it mismatches; implement the four CKPRST paragraphs (write/rewrite/read of CHECKPOINT-FILE with file-status checks).

                 10  CKR-PROGRAM-ID      PIC X(8).
                 10  CKR-RUN-DATE        PIC X(8).
             05  CKR-DATA                PIC X(400).

findings.title: GnuCOBOL parity tests for copybook codecs and record lengths
findings.description:
##### Artifact

Pytest module (skipped unless `cobc` is on PATH, line 15 via conftest) that compiles COBOL fixtures and checks COBOL-written bytes decode in Python and vice versa for two compiler dialects (39-78), checks the suite's POSREC/TRNREC COMP-3 parity (81-102), and checks LENGTH OF every suite copybook against the Python layout (108-124). conftest runs `cobc` via `shutil.which` with argument lists and no shell.

##### Bears on

SA-11 developer testing evidence (functional/data-format testing).

##### Limits

No security-focused tests (authorization denial, audit writes, lockout) and no CI configuration in the repo; tests silently skip when cobc is missing.

snippets.commentary: parity test for the repo's own copybooks.
snippets.code:
def test_suite_copybooks_poswrt_parity(tmp_path):
      """The repo's own POSREC/TRNREC (COMP-3 money fields) written by COBOL, read by Python."""
      exe = compile_cobol(COBOL_FIXTURES / "POSWRT.cbl", tmp_path, "ibm")
      run_cobol(exe, tmp_path)
      pos = load_layout(COPYBOOKS / "common" / "POSREC.cpy", dialect=GNUCOBOL_IBM)
      trn = load_layout(COPYBOOKS / "common" / "TRNREC.cpy", dialect=GNUCOBOL_IBM)
      p = [pos.decode(r) for r in iter_records((tmp_path / "positions.dat").read_bytes(), pos.length)]
      t = [trn.decode(r) for r in iter_records((tmp_path / "transactions.dat").read_bytes(), trn.length)]
      assert [r["POS-QUANTITY"] for r in p] == [Decimal("1234567.8912"), Decimal("99999999999.9999")]
      assert p[0]["POS-COST-BASIS"] == Decimal("-98765432109.87")
      assert p[0]["POS-MARKET-VALUE"] == Decimal("0.01")
      assert p[1]["POS-MARKET-VALUE"] == Decimal("-9999999999999.99")
      assert (p[0]["POS-STATUS"], p[1]["POS-STATUS"]) == ("A", "C")
      # COBOL COMPUTE without ROUNDED truncates 100.5 * 19.99 = 2008.995 to the V99 scale.
      assert Decimal("100.5") * Decimal("19.99") == Decimal("2008.995")
      assert t[0]["TRN-AMOUNT"] == Decimal("2008.99")
      assert t[1]["TRN-AMOUNT"] == Decimal("-12.50")
      assert t[1]["TRN-TYPE"] == "FE" and t[1]["TRN-STATUS"] == "R"
      # Python port writes the same records -> byte-identical -> diff harness reports MATCH.
      again = b"".join(pos.encode(r) for r in p)
      assert again == (tmp_path / "positions.dat").read_bytes()
      assert diff_bytes(pos, (tmp_path / "positions.dat").read_bytes(), again).ok

snippets.commentary: cobc located via shutil.which and invoked with argument lists.
snippets.code:
COBC = shutil.which("cobc")
  requires_cobc = pytest.mark.skipif(COBC is None, reason="GnuCOBOL (cobc) not installed")
  
  
  def copybook_includes() -> list[str]:
      dirs = [COBOL_FIXTURES] + [d for d in COPYBOOKS.iterdir() if d.is_dir()]
      return [f"-I{d}" for d in dirs]
  
  
  def compile_cobol(source: Path, workdir: Path, std: str = "default", extra: list[str] = ()) -> Path:
      exe = workdir / source.stem.lower()
      cmd = [COBC, "-x", "-w", f"-std={std}", *extra, *copybook_includes(), "-o", str(exe), str(source)]
      r = subprocess.run(cmd, capture_output=True, text=True)
      if r.returncode:
          raise RuntimeError(f"cobc failed: {' '.join(cmd)}\n{r.stdout}\n{r.stderr}")
      return exe
  
  
  def run_cobol(exe: Path, workdir: Path) -> str:
      r = subprocess.run([str(exe)], cwd=workdir, capture_output=True, text=True)
      if r.returncode:
          raise RuntimeError(f"{exe.name} failed rc={r.returncode}\n{r.stdout}\n{r.stderr}")
      return r.stdout

findings.title: PORTDEF deletes portfolio master with error masking; redefine falls outside SYSIN
findings.description:
##### Overview

The job unconditionally deletes the PORTFOLIO.MASTER.FILE cluster and resets MAXCC to 0, then the DEFINE CLUSTER statements follow a `//*` line that ends the in-stream SYSIN, so they are not passed to IDCAMS; the job can leave the master deleted with a clean return code.

##### Applicability

SC-24 (fail to a known state) and CM-6 (documented, correct configuration of the master data store).

##### Evidence

PORTDEF.jcl 18-22: IDCAMS SYSIN with DELETE and SET MAXCC = 0. Line 23 `//*` in columns 1-2 terminates the DD * data, so 27-33 (DEFINE CLUSTER) are parsed as JCL, not IDCAMS input.

##### Impact

- Running this job destroys the master file and may not recreate it, while reporting success.
- No audit record of the deletion.
- Inferred from standard JES in-stream rules; validate by submitting in a test LPAR.
findings.recommendation: Put the DEFINE CLUSTER statements inside the SYSIN stream (remove the `//*` lines between DELETE and DEFINE), use `IF LASTCC = 8 THEN SET MAXCC = 0` only for the not-found case, and require explicit approval before delete.

snippets.commentary: delete with MAXCC reset, then comment line ending SYSIN before DEFINE.

findings.title: Core portfolio tables and views defined with no GRANTs or authorization documentation
findings.description:
##### Overview

PORTFOLIO_MASTER, INVESTMENT_POSITIONS, TRANSACTION_HISTORY and the two views are created with no GRANT statements, so the repo defines no approved authorisations for the main customer tables, unlike ERRLOG/POSHIST which grant role-specific privileges.

findings.title: PORTMSTR create and delete leave no audit record; update audit broken
findings.description:
##### Overview
PORTMSTR creates (`WRITE`), updates (`REWRITE`) and deletes (`DELETE`) portfolio master records. Only the update path calls the audit routine. `2100-LOG-PORTFOLIO-UPDATE` refers to data items PORTMSTR never defines and records no real before-image, and the AUDPROC return code is ignored.

##### Applicability
AU-2/AU-12 require audit records for the defined events. Create, update and delete of the authoritative portfolio master are the core audited events in this system (the AUDITLOG layout defines CREATE/UPDATE/DELETE actions). AU-3 requires the record content, and AU-5 requires a response when logging fails.

##### Evidence
- Lines 115-136 (create, `WRITE` at 126) and 209-226 (delete, `DELETE` at 215) contain no `CALL 'AUDPROC'`.
- Line 206: update performs `2100-LOG-PORTFOLIO-UPDATE`. In that paragraph (lines 268-288), `LS-AUDIT-REQUEST`, `LS-SYSTEM-ID`, `USERID`, `TERMINAL-ID`, `WS-BEFORE-IMAGE`, `PORT-ACCOUNT-NO`, `PORT-RECORD` and the other `LS-*` targets are not declared in PORTMSTR's WORKING-STORAGE or LINKAGE (lines 41-80). The before-image is never captured before the `REWRITE` at 194.
- Line 287: the call result (`LS-RETURN-CODE` in AUDPROC) is never checked.
- Lines 243-263 duplicate the `2100-` paragraph prefix with further undefined items, which suggests template code that was never integrated.

##### Impact
- Portfolio creation and deletion, including irreversible removal of master records, leave no trace of who did what.
- Updates cannot produce a valid before/after record, and failed audit writes go unnoticed.
- Assumption: callers of PORTMSTR do not write their own audit records. None was found in this batch.
findings.recommendation: Declare the AUDPROC request area (matching AUDPROC's LS-AUDIT-REQUEST) and a before-image buffer in PORTMSTR. findings.title: Denied or failed inquiry access attempts are never written to AUDITLOG
findings.description:
##### Overview
INQONLN asks SECMGR to write an access record (`SEC-REQUEST-TYPE 'L'`) only when both validation and authorization succeed. Denied and failed attempts leave no audit record. When the audit write itself fails, the data has already been displayed, and the only response is an error routine and RETURN.

##### Applicability
AU-2/AU-12 call for audit records of the defined event types, and access-control decisions (successful and unsuccessful) are standard ones. AU-5 requires a response to audit logging failures. INQONLN is the code that decides which online access events get recorded.

##### Evidence
- Lines 151-169: the `'L'` log request sits inside two nested `IF SEC-RESPONSE-CODE = 0` blocks. A non-zero result from validate (`'V'`) or authorize (`'A'`) skips logging entirely.
- Lines 82-88: the only handling for a non-zero code is `P900-ERROR-ROUTINE` (ERRHNDL, a warning) plus RETURN. These lines also cover an audit failure ('Audit logging failed' from SECMGR), which arrives after the inquiry output was sent.

##### Impact
- No record exists of unauthorized attempts to view portfolio or history data, so security reviews of failed access are impossible.
- An audit-write failure does not stop disclosure and raises no alert beyond the ERRHNDL warning.
- Not verified: whether ERRHNDL's DB2 error log is reviewed or alerted on (it logs the message at warning severity).
findings.recommendation: Call SECMGR 'L' on every decision, passing an outcome indicator (granted, denied validation, denied authorization) so AUDITLOG records failed attempts too. Do the log write before the inquiry, and when the audit write fails, deny the inquiry and raise an ERR-ABEND/ERR-CRITICAL condition through ERRHNDL instead of a warning.

findings.title: INQONLN dispatches portfolio and history inquiries before running SECMGR checks
findings.description:
##### Overview
In each loop of `P100-PROCESS-REQUEST`, INQONLN runs the requested function (LINK to INQPORT/INQHIST, which read and SEND position/history data) and only afterwards calls `P050-SECURITY-CHECK`. The SECMGR validate/authorize decision therefore cannot stop the disclosure it is meant to gate. Any CICS transaction-level security on PINQ (RACF/ESM, outside this repo) is not visible here.

##### Applicability
AC-3 requires that approved authorizations are enforced before logical access to information is granted. INQONLN is the only entry program of transaction PINQ (`src/cics/PORTDFN.csd`) and is where the application's own authorization (SECMGR resource `INQONLN`/`READ`) is invoked. Signon and transaction-attach security are handled by CICS/ESM configuration outside the repo.

##### Evidence
- Lines 62-77: the EVALUATE on `WS-COMMAREA-FUNCTION` performs `P300-PORTFOLIO-INQUIRY` / `P400-HISTORY-INQUIRY` right away.
- Lines 79-88: `P050-SECURITY-CHECK` runs only after that, and a non-zero `SEC-RESPONSE-CODE` causes a RETURN once the data has already been sent.
- Lines 101-117: the LINKs pass the terminal-supplied COMMAREA (account number) to INQPORT/INQHIST, which display the data (INQPORT line 46-52 SEND MAP).

```
RECEIVE MAP --> LINK INQPORT/INQHIST --> SEND MAP (data shown) --> SECMGR V/A --> deny => RETURN
```

##### Impact
- Portfolio positions and transaction history for any account number typed on the screen are shown to users who would fail the SECMGR `AUTHFILE` check.
- The application-level access decision has no effect on disclosure. Only ESM transaction security (not verifiable here) gates PINQ.
- Assumption: INQPORT/INQHIST do no checks of their own. I confirmed this for INQPORT, and INQHIST has no SECMGR call.
findings.recommendation: Run P050-SECURITY-CHECK right after RECEIVE MAP and before the EVALUATE dispatch. Perform the INQP/INQH branches only when validate and authorize both return 0, and on denial send a generic error map and stop without LINKing to INQPORT/INQHIST. Initialize WS-SECURITY-REQUEST (including SEC-RESPONSE-CODE) before each check.

                      PERFORM P200-DISPLAY-MENU

                 WHEN 'INQP'

                         THRU P300-EXIT
                 WHEN 'INQH'
                      PERFORM P400-HISTORY-INQUIRY
                         THRU P400-EXIT
                 WHEN 'EXIT'
                      SET SESSION-TERMINATED TO TRUE
                 WHEN OTHER
                      PERFORM P900-ERROR-ROUTINE
                         THRU P900-EXIT
             END-EVALUATE.

findings.title: SECMGR user validation compares ASSIGN USERID against caller-copied USERID
findings.description:
##### Artifact
`P100-VALIDATE-USER` (lines 57-75) issues `EXEC CICS ASSIGN USERID` and compares the result to `SEC-USER-ID`. The caller INQONLN (lines 142-144) filled that field from the same `ASSIGN USERID`. No password, authenticator, ESM `VERIFY`/`SIGNON`, or failed-attempt counter appears anywhere in the program. User identity comes from whatever CICS signon established for the task.

##### Bears on
IA-2 (unique identification and authentication), AC-7 (invalid logon attempt limit and lockout), and IA-5 (authenticator management). These lines hand authentication to the CICS region's signon and external security manager (e.g. RACF): password policy, the consecutive-failure limit and lockout must be evidenced from the ESM and CICS SIT configuration (SEC=YES, signon transaction), which are not in this repository.

##### Limits
The code does not show whether PINQ requires a signed-on user (rather than the CICS default user), or any ESM settings.

             EXEC CICS ASSIGN
                       USERID(WS-USER-ID)
                       RESP(SEC-RESPONSE-CODE)
             END-EXEC.

                ELSE

                     TO SEC-ERROR-INFO
                   MOVE 8 TO SEC-RESPONSE-CODE
                END-IF
             ELSE
                MOVE 'Unable to obtain user credentials' 
                  TO SEC-ERROR-INFO
                MOVE 12 TO SEC-RESPONSE-CODE
             END-IF.

findings.title: INQPORT returns positions for any COMMAREA account number without ownership check
findings.description:
##### Overview
INQPORT reads POSFILE using the account number from the COMMAREA, which INQONLN fills straight from the terminal map, and sends the record to the screen. Nothing checks whether the signed-on user may see that account. The only application authorization in the flow (SECMGR) works at program level (`INQONLN`/`READ`) and runs after INQPORT, per the INQONLN finding.

##### Applicability
AC-3 requires access to information to follow approved authorizations, and AC-6 requires access limited to what the user needs. Client portfolio positions are per-account data, and INQPORT is the component that reads and discloses them. Record-level dataset security in the ESM (outside the repo) cannot restrict by account inside one VSAM file.

##### Evidence
- Lines 58-59: the COMMAREA is copied in as-is.
- Lines 63-70: `INQCOM-ACCOUNT-NO` becomes the RIDFLD for `READ FILE('POSFILE')`. There is no format check and no lookup of the user's entitlements.
- Lines 80-84: the record is sent to the terminal.
- SECMGR lines 57-67 (P200) authorize on `RESOURCE = 'INQONLN'` only, never on the account.

##### Impact
- Any user with access to PINQ can list another client's positions (units, cost basis, market value) by entering that client's account number.
- Assumption: no ESM or account-level entitlement table outside the repo is consulted. Nothing in the repo references one.
findings.recommendation: Before the POSFILE read, validate the account number's format, then authorize the signed-on user (EXEC CICS ASSIGN USERID) for that specific account. Do this through a SECMGR 'A' request with the account as the resource, an entitlement table, or EXEC CICS QUERY SECURITY on an account-level profile. Return a generic not-authorized message on denial and log the decision.

             EXEC CICS HANDLE CONDITION
                       ERROR(P999-ERROR-ROUTINE)
                       NOTFND(P900-NOT-FOUND)
             END-EXEC.

             EXIT.

             MOVE WS-COMMAREA-ACCOUNT-NO 
               TO POSITION-ACCOUNT OF WS-POSITION-RECORD.

                       INTO(WS-POSITION-RECORD)

             END-EXEC.

findings.title: PORTUPDT batch REWRITEs portfolio master without any audit record
findings.description:
##### Overview
PORTUPDT applies sequential update transactions (status, client name, total value) to the portfolio master with `REWRITE`. It writes no audit record and does not update the record's own `PORT-LAST-USER`/`PORT-LAST-MAINT` fields, so each change leaves no who/what/before/after trace.

##### Applicability
AU-2/AU-12 require audit records for the defined event types, and AU-3 requires their content. Changes to the authoritative portfolio master, including client name and holdings value, are audited event types per the AUDITLOG UPDATE action, and AUDPROC exists for this purpose.

##### Evidence
- Lines 49-69: `2200-APPLY-UPDATE` overwrites fields and `REWRITE`s with no AUDPROC call and no before-image saved.
- The only output is SYSOUT counters (lines 77-78).
- The JCL (`src/jcl/portfolio/PORTUPDT.jcl`) allocates no audit dataset.

##### Impact
- Bulk changes to client names, account status and valuations are untraceable to a job, a user, or prior values.
- Assumption: no external SMF/ESM dataset-level logging is relied on for record-level change history. That would record dataset access only, not field changes.
findings.recommendation: Before each REWRITE, copy the read record to a before-image. After the REWRITE, call AUDPROC with system/user (job/RACF user), program PORTUPDT, action UPDATE, SUCC/FAIL status, the PORT-KEY, and the before/after images. Set PORT-LAST-USER/PORT-LAST-MAINT, check AUDPROC's return code, and stop with a non-zero RC if auditing fails.
findings.note: Shared root cause: batch portfolio-master maintenance programs mutate VSAM/DB2 records without routing through the AUDPROC audit service (only PORTMSTR/PORTTRAN call it). One pattern fix (call AUDPROC with before/after images and job/user identity on every add/update/delete; allocate the audit DD in JCL) covers members: PORTADD sfind-d0ef075d1daf4126a5edf412faff43c0, PORTMSTR sfind-eededaeaead042ce9fb094acf5f198db, HISTLD00 sfind-8d465df29f3a43f099f1376b885c2fe5, RCVPRC00 sfind-cc4d4e4cea8c43709a10dca7875e1a95, PORTUPDT.jcl (merged duplicate sfind-f77f9520a98b4c47a4bc7d2b9f51a7f4; also duplicate sfind-00d6011e133e426d927c68c67d6c6359). findings.description:
##### Overview
`P200-CHECK-AUTH` selects `COUNT(*)` INTO `:WS-DB2-AREA`, the 01-level group that holds the SQLCA, and then makes the grant decision with `IF WS-DB2-AREA > 0`. That is an alphanumeric group comparison, not a test of an integer count. The access decision does not reliably reflect AUTHFILE contents and may fail open. The exact runtime result depends on precompiler/compiler handling, which I could not run.

##### Applicability
AC-3 requires enforcement of approved authorizations. SECMGR is the application's central access-decision routine for the online inquiry programs.

##### Evidence
- Lines 1-3 of the working storage (file lines 14-15): `WS-DB2-AREA` contains only `INCLUDE SQLCA`.
- Lines 78-85: the COUNT is written into that group, so the SQLCA itself is overlaid.
- Lines 87-95: `WS-DB2-AREA > 0` compares the group, which starts with SQLCAID text, against zero as alphanumeric. A non-blank character string compares greater than '0', so any `SQLCODE = 0` result can come out as a grant whatever the count is.
- Lines 41-51: the EVALUATE has no `WHEN OTHER`, so an unrecognised request type returns with whatever `SEC-RESPONSE-CODE` the caller passed in (INQONLN never initializes it).

##### Impact
- Users with no AUTHFILE row may be authorized for `INQONLN READ`.
- Unknown request types are not denied by default.
- Not verified: actual compiled behaviour. Validation should test a user absent from AUTHFILE.
findings.recommendation: Declare a dedicated `WS-AUTH-COUNT PIC S9(9) COMP` host variable, select COUNT(*) INTO it, and grant only when `SQLCODE = 0 AND WS-AUTH-COUNT > 0`. Add `WHEN OTHER` that sets SEC-RESPONSE-CODE to a deny value, and initialize SEC-RESPONSE-CODE to non-zero at entry so all paths fail closed.

snippets.commentary: The host-variable target is the SQLCA group, not an integer field.
snippets.code:
WORKING-STORAGE SECTION.
         01  WS-DB2-AREA.

snippets.commentary: COUNT(*) goes into the SQLCA group, and the grant is decided by a group comparison.

P200-CHECK-AUTH.
             EXEC SQL
                  SELECT COUNT(*)
                  INTO :WS-DB2-AREA
                  FROM AUTHFILE
                  WHERE USER_ID = :SEC-USER-ID
                    AND RESOURCE = :SEC-RESOURCE-NAME
                    AND ACCESS_TYPE = :SEC-ACCESS-TYPE
             END-EXEC.
             
             EVALUATE SQLCODE
                 WHEN 0
                      IF WS-DB2-AREA > 0
                         MOVE 0 TO SEC-RESPONSE-CODE
                      ELSE
                         MOVE 'Access denied' 
                           TO SEC-ERROR-INFO
                         MOVE 8 TO SEC-RESPONSE-CODE
                      END-IF
                 WHEN OTHER
                      MOVE 'Authorization check failed' 
                        TO SEC-ERROR-INFO
                      MOVE 12 TO SEC-RESPONSE-CODE
             END-EVALUATE.
         P200-EXIT.

findings.title: SECMGR AUDITLOG insert omits event outcome and accessed object
findings.description:
##### Overview
`P300-LOG-ACCESS` inserts timestamp, user, terminal, transaction, program and access type into AUDITLOG. It records no event outcome (success/failure) and no identity of the object accessed (account number). Because it is only called after a grant, it also cannot tell success from failure.

##### Applicability
AU-3 requires audit records to establish the type of event, when, where, source, outcome, and the identity of the individuals or subjects/objects involved. SECMGR writes the only online access audit record for the inquiry transaction.

##### Evidence
- Lines 116-124: the insert column list has no STATUS/OUTCOME column and no account or portfolio key. `PROGRAM` takes `SEC-RESOURCE-NAME`, which the caller always sets to the constant 'INQONLN'.
- The shared audit layout (`src/copybook/common/AUDITLOG.cpy`, `AUD-STATUS`, `AUD-ACCOUNT-NO`) already defines both fields, and this insert does not fill them.

##### Impact
- AUDITLOG entries cannot show which client account was viewed or whether access was granted, so audit review cannot reconstruct a disclosure.
- Assumption: the DB2 AUDITLOG table has, or can be given, status and key columns. The DDL was not part of this batch.
findings.recommendation: Add outcome (SUCC/FAIL plus reason) and the accessed account/portfolio key to the SECMGR request area and AUDITLOG insert. Have callers log every decision, not only grants.
