findings.title: PORTUPDT applies update-file values to master with no validity checks
findings.description:
##### Overview
Values from UPDTFILE are moved straight into the master record without type, range or domain checks, then REWRITTEN.

##### Applicability
SI-10 requires validity checks on information inputs. The batch update file is an external input to the authoritative portfolio master.

##### Evidence
- Line 53: a 50-byte `UPDT-NEW-VALUE` is truncated into one-byte `PORT-STATUS` with no check against the A/C/S 88-levels.
- Line 55: client name is copied without a blank or content check.
- Lines 57-58: an alphanumeric value is MOVEd to a numeric field with no `IS NUMERIC` test, which can yield garbage or a data exception on the COMP-3 `PORT-TOTAL-VALUE`.
- Lines 49-59: an action code outside S/V/N falls through the EVALUATE and still REWRITEs.

##### Impact
- Invalid statuses, blank names or corrupt valuations can be persisted to the master file used by online inquiry and reporting.
findings.recommendation: Validate each update before applying it: status must be one of the PORTFLIO 88-level values, the name must be non-blank, the value must pass an `IS NUMERIC`/`FUNCTION TEST-NUMVAL` check and a range check before conversion, and the action code must be valid (add WHEN OTHER). Reject and count invalid records without REWRITE.

                 WHEN UPDT-VALUE

findings.title: Portfolio deletion continues after audit write failure

##### Overview

When the audit WRITE fails, PORTDEL only DISPLAYs a message and continues deleting records; it neither stops nor raises the job return code.

##### Applicability

AU-5 requires alerting and a defined response on audit logging failure; deletions are performed after the delete is committed to the master file.

PORTDEL.cbl lines 177-181: after WRITE AUDIT-RECORD, a non-'00' status only triggers DISPLAY; the delete at the caller (line ~160) has already happened and processing continues. The audit dataset is a plain sequential file with DISP=MOD (PORTDEL.jcl line 14).

findings.title: DISCONNECT-FROM-DB2 commits unconditionally regardless of unit-of-work state
findings.description:
##### Overview

The shared disconnect paragraph issues COMMIT WORK with no check of SQLCODE or caller status, and CONNECT failure only rolls back and logs without stopping the caller. Callers that reach disconnect after an unchecked failure will commit partial work.

##### Applicability

SC-24 (fail in a known state) and SI-7 (information integrity) apply to the common DB2 procedures copied into DB2CONN, DB2CMT, DB2ERR, DB2STAT and HISTLD00.

##### Evidence

DBPROC.cpy lines 36-43: COMMIT WORK then CONNECT RESET, with no condition and no SQLCODE check on the COMMIT. Lines 26-33: on connect failure, DB2-ERROR-ROUTINE runs but control returns to the caller with no abort flag set. Lines 46-57 roll back only when a caller invokes CHECK-SQL-STATUS.

##### Impact

- Partial updates to DB2 history/position tables can be committed on an error path, diverging from VSAM.
- A failed COMMIT is silently ignored.
- Did not trace every caller to confirm one actually reaches disconnect after an unhandled error.
findings.recommendation: Commit only when a success flag set by the caller is true (otherwise ROLLBACK), check SQLCODE after COMMIT and route failures to DB2-ERROR-ROUTINE, and set a fatal return code on connect failure so callers terminate.
findings.note: Same pattern (disconnect issues unconditional COMMIT) in DB2CONN.cbl 2000-DISCONNECT sfind-dbd2209d80d34c0ba1764351f552245c, which has its own copy of the logic; DBPROC.cpy is COPYed into DB2ERR, DB2STAT, DB2CMT, DB2CONN and HISTLD00. Fix both: commit only on a known-good unit of work, otherwise ROLLBACK.

findings.title: PORTPLAN bind uses wildcard PKLIST, RETAIN, VALIDATE(RUN), no OWNER
findings.description:
##### Overview

The DB2 plan used by the online system binds any package in collection-wildcard `*.PORTPKG.*`, retains existing EXECUTE grants on replace, and defers authorization checks to run time, with no OWNER or QUALIFIER specified.

##### Applicability

CM-6 (documented, restrictive configuration settings) and AC-6 (least privilege) apply to the plan executed by CICS DB2ENTRY PORTDB2. DB2 GRANTs themselves are outside the repo.

##### Evidence

PORTPLAN.sql line 2 binds PKLIST(*.PORTPKG.*), lines 3-4 ACTION(REPLACE) RETAIN, line 5 VALIDATE(RUN); there is no OWNER/QUALIFIER clause, so ownership defaults to the binder and unqualified table names resolve to the binder's ID.

##### Impact

- Any package bound into a PORTPKG collection on any location becomes executable under the plan's authority.
- Missing-privilege errors surface only at run time rather than blocking the bind.
- Plan ownership depends on who ran the bind, not a controlled ID.
findings.recommendation: Bind with an explicit PKLIST(location.PORTPKG.pkgname,...) or at least a fixed location, add OWNER(<controlled authid>) and QUALIFIER(<schema>), use VALIDATE(BIND), and review RETAIN so EXECUTE grants are re-approved on replace.

snippets.commentary: Full bind statement with wildcard PKLIST, RETAIN, VALIDATE(RUN), no OWNER/QUALIFIER.
snippets.code:
-- DB2 Plan Definition for Portfolio System
  BIND PLAN PORTPLAN
       PKLIST(*.PORTPKG.*)
       ACTION(REPLACE)
       RETAIN
       VALIDATE(RUN)
       ISOLATION(CS)
       ACQUIRE(USE)
       RELEASE(COMMIT)

findings.title: Inquiry-only POSFILE defined with ADD(YES) though no program writes it
findings.description:
##### Overview

The CICS FILE definition for the position VSAM cluster permits record ADD from any transaction in the region, while the only online consumer performs a READ. The capability is unused but available.

##### Applicability

CM-7 / AC-6 require the system to provide only mission-essential capabilities and only the accesses needed. The CSD is the repo's in-scope configuration for the online inquiry system; RACF file-level profiles (if any) are outside the repo.

##### Evidence

PORTDFN.csd lines 69-79 define POSFILE with ADD(YES) alongside READ(YES)/BROWSE(YES). The only online reference to POSFILE is `EXEC CICS READ FILE('POSFILE')` in INQPORT.cbl line 72; no WRITE FILE/REWRITE/DELETE FILE exists under src/programs/online.

##### Impact

- Any program in the region (or a future/rogue program) can insert position records into the authoritative holdings master via CICS without a code path requiring it.
- Assumes no out-of-repo programs need online ADD; not verified against the running region.
findings.recommendation: Set ADD(NO) on POSFILE (keeping READ/BROWSE) so the inquiry region cannot add position records.
findings.note: Merged duplicate: sfind-9e124695e6a3486ca6df303499c58fdc. Downgraded to LOW (CM-7 hygiene; no writer exists).

findings.title: Python tooling has no dependency manifest; pytest and cobc unpinned

##### Overview

The Python parity tooling and tests import pytest and invoke GnuCOBOL `cobc`, but the repo contains no requirements, pyproject, lock file or version constraint for either.

##### Applicability

findings.title: SECMGR security program shares USER key and group with application programs
findings.description:
##### Overview

SECMGR, which performs user validation, AUTHFILE authorization checks and AUDITLOG writes, is defined identically to ordinary inquiry programs (EXECKEY(USER), same group), and the PINQ transaction carries no resource/command security attributes. Region-level storage protection (SIT STGPROT/TRANISO) is outside the repo and may mitigate this.

##### Applicability

SC-3 requires isolating security functions from non-security functions; AC-3/AC-6(1) require enforced access to security functions. The CSD is the in-repo definition of these programs and transactions; SIT parameters and RACF XTRAN/XRES classes must come from region configuration.

##### Evidence

PORTDFN.csd lines 56-61 define SECMGR with EXECKEY(USER) like INQONLN/INQPORT etc. (lines 14-54). PINQ (lines 6-11) specifies no RESSEC(YES) or CMDSEC(YES). SECMGR.cbl lines 41-52 show it performs validation, authorization and audit for callers that LINK to it with a caller-supplied COMMAREA.

##### Impact

- Security decision and audit logic is not separated by key or definition from user programs; any user-key program can overwrite its storage if storage protection is not enabled.
- CICS-level resource checks are not requested, so access enforcement relies entirely on application LINKs to SECMGR.
- Could not verify STGPROT/TRANISO/XRES settings of the region.
findings.recommendation: Define SECMGR with EXECKEY(CICS) (or in a separately controlled group), add RESSEC(YES) and CMDSEC(YES) to PINQ, and document required SIT STGPROT=YES/TRANISO=YES for the region.
findings.note: Merged duplicate: sfind-807b461c1bc146a7a3eef9cc641795e6. Partly depends on region SIT STGPROT/TRANISO and RACF XTRAN/XRES (platform, out of scope).
